title: 'Locked' trade prices for all 368 SKUs are public in the JS bundle and the anonymous Supabase API
location: All routes (e.g. #/product/1 → price block 'Sign in / Wholesale pricing is visible to approved trade accounts'); Supabase GET /rest/v1/products; production JS bundle
evidence: While signed out, the storefront itself calls GET /rest/v1/products?select=*&active=eq.true, which returns 200 with 368 rows. All 368 include `price` (for example id 1 Swisher Sweets cigarillos 41.76, id 2 White Owl 84.34). The page shows 'LOCKED · Sign in for pricing' on cards and 'Sign in' on the product page. The static catalog shipped to every browser has the same data: /src/data/products.js holds 368 `price:` fields, and the built dist/assets/index-CvpKVAyY.js has 368 `price:` literals. Anyone can call import('/src/data/products.js') and read PRODUCTS[0].price = 41.76. RLS policy products_public_read (`using (active = true)`) exposes every column, including price, to the anon role. pricing_tiers_public_read (`using (true)`) also publishes the tier discount table. The Trade terms page says prices 'are not for publication'. Approval gating in the UI and server-side pricing in submit_quote are now fixed; the exposure itself is not.
fix: Remove price from the bundled static catalog (products.js, build-seed output) and from anon-readable columns. Revoke anon SELECT on products.price (a column privilege, or a view without price), and expose prices only through an RPC/view that checks auth and approved status, applying the tier server-side (rls_policies.sql:39, 89; launch_order_boundaries.sql:47, 111; useCatalog.js:19).

title: Search has no results page: Enter opens the first product and the result count stops at 10
location: Header search (.aw-search form) on every route
evidence: getSearchMatches(products, query, limit = 10) (App.jsx:53) cuts the list at 10, and the dropdown label shows hits.length. So 'cigar' reads '10 results' although 30 products match, and 'tobacco' reads '10 results' for 68 matches. There is no 'See all results' row and no search route. Pressing Enter on 'cigar' ran submitSearch (App.jsx:437-440), which went straight to #/product/5 ('4K's cigarillos') and cleared the query. Pressing Enter on 'xyz123' or on a 1-character query does nothing and shows no message. Clicking the magnifier with an empty field does nothing.
fix:
1. Add a search route: in parseHash (App.jsx:165) map '#/search/<encodeURIComponent(q)>' to {page:'search', q}, and add the reverse in routeToHash (App.jsx:177).
2. Create src/pages/support/SearchPage.jsx. It calls getSearchMatches(products, q, Infinity), shows the heading 'N results for “q”' and renders the hits with ProductCard in the same grid the category page uses. Its empty state links to #/catalog.
3. Change submitSearch so that whenever query.trim().length >= 2 it calls navigate({page:'search', q: query.trim()}), and keep the query in the box.
4. In the dropdown, run the matcher with limit Infinity, display slice(0, 8), and label it 'Showing 8 of 30'. Add a final row 'See all 30 results for “cigar” →' that navigates to the search route.
5. When the query is shorter than 2 characters and the user presses Enter, show the helper line 'Type at least 2 characters'.

title: Filter, sort and search state is not in the URL and is lost on Back and reload
location: #/category/<DEPT> → sort select, 'Search in <dept>' box, Featured checkboxes
evidence: On #/category/CANDIES I set Sort = 'Name: A to Z', checked Bestsellers and searched 'bar' ('Showing 3 of 58 items'). I opened a product (#/product/171) and pressed Back. The page came back as sort=featured, q='', no checkboxes ticked, 'Showing 58 of 58 items'. Reloading after setting sort=name-desc and q='gum' also reset everything to featured with no search. The hash only ever holds #/category/CANDIES, so a filtered or sorted view can't be bookmarked or shared. The sub-line is the only state kept in the URL.
fix: Store category search text, sort and Featured/tag filters in the URL query (for example #/category/TOBACCO?q=&sort=&tags=), and read them back on mount, so Back from a product page, reload and shared links restore the state. Restore the scroll position when returning (App.jsx:851-889).

title: "Choose variant" on a bare cart line loses the reorder quantity and leaves an unfixable line that blocks checkout
location: Cart drawer and #/quote → line with no variant (created by account Reorder / addLines) → 'Choose variant' link → #/product/<id>
evidence: Seeded aw-cart {"1":12,"14":2} at 1440×900. (1) The header badge reads 'Cart 14'. The drawer line reads 'Swisher Sweets cigarillos AW-SS · Choose a variant' with a 'Choose variant' link and no quantity. (2) 'Choose variant' closes the drawer and opens #/product/1. All 8 chips have aria-pressed=false, and the page says 'Already in quote: 12'. (3) Choosing Red then 'Add to quote' gives storage {"1":12,"14":2,"1::red":1}, and the badge becomes 15. (4) On #/quote the lines are the bare 'Swisher Sweets cigarillos AW-SS Choose a variant before submitting', Kite ×2 and '— Red AW-SS-RED 1'. The total reads '15 units', the form's submit button is disabled=true, and it shows the alert 'Choose a variant for every product that has more than one.' 'Choose variant' on #/quote opens #/product/1 again, still showing 'Already in quote: 12'. Evidence: screenshots/vcart__drawer-bare-line.jpg, screenshots/vcart__quote-bare-line-blocked.jpg
fix: (a) In src/App.jsx:9, add parseLineKey to the import from './lib/lines.js'. Next to removeLine (App.jsx:262), add `const chooseLineVariant = (bareKey, variant) => setCart(c => { const n = { ...c }; const q = Number(n[bareKey]) || 0; delete n[bareKey]; if (!variant || !(q > 0)) return n; const k = lineKey(parseLineKey(bareKey).productId, variant); n[k] = (Number(n[k]) || 0) + q; return n; });`. Pass it to CartDrawer and QuotePage. (b) In src/lib/lines.js:159-169, add `variants` to the bare-line object. (c) In CartDrawer (App.jsx:1406-1408) and QuotePage (App.jsx:1252-1254), replace the 'Choose variant' button with `<select aria-label={`Choose variant for ${it.name}`} defaultValue="" onChange={e => chooseLineVariant(it.lineKey, e.target.value)}><option value="" disabled>Choose variant…</option>{it.variants.map(v => <option key={v} value={v}>{v}</option>)}</select>`. (d) Change the bare-line <small> text in both places to `${it.qty} units · choose a variant`. (e) In ProductPage (App.jsx:1068), change to `const qty = (choiceRequired && !selected) ? 0 : (cart[key] || 0);` so the bare-line quantity is not shown as 'Already in quote: 12'.

title: Quantity can only change one unit per tap and has no bounds/integer validation
location: Cart drawer .qty stepper, #/quote .checkout-line stepper, #/product/<id> .qty-stepper, product card .card-stepper
evidence: Every quantity control is a static <b> between − and + buttons (App.jsx:1411, 1257, 1120, 836). Nothing accepts typed input. To order 50 cases, a buyer must click + 49 times per line, in both the product page and the cart. For a wholesale site with a server-side limit of 100000 per line (launch_order_boundaries.sql:72), this is the main friction in the order flow. Measured: the drawer stepper is 40×40 buttons around a 34px-wide read-only number.
fix: Replace the +/− only steppers (PDP, cards, cart drawer, #/quote, Quick Reorder) with a numeric input (inputmode='numeric') flanked by −/+. Clamp to integers between 1 and 100,000 to match the server limit, disable − at 1, and validate on hydration and before submit (App.jsx:239-248, 834, 1118-1122, 1255-1259, 1409-1413).

also_seen.location: #/product/<id> → .qty-stepper
also_seen.evidence: The stepper is two buttons around a <b> (App.jsx:1118-1122) with no <input>, so values like 0, -1, abc or 99999 cannot be typed. The downside is that a wholesale buyer ordering 40 cases must tap + 39 times. My test needed 120 taps to reach 121. There is no upper bound (Math.max only on the low side), no minimum order or step, and '−' stays enabled at 1 and does nothing on tap.

also_seen.location: #/product/<id> 'Quantity to add' stepper; card steppers; cart drawer and #/quote line quantities
also_seen.evidence: Every quantity control is − / {qty} / +, with no input. Getting a wholesale quantity of 48 cases takes 47 presses of '+', which is a real burden for switch, voice-control and tremor users (voice users can't say 'type 48'). The value lives in a element, so it isn't editable or readable as a form value.

also_seen.location: #/product/<id> quantity stepper, cart/checkout steppers, #/account Quick Reorder qty, stored cart
also_seen.evidence: addLine/addLines (App.jsx:239-260) and the product stepper (App.jsx:1121) have no maximum, and there is no typed quantity field on the product page (reaching 120 units takes 119 clicks on '+'). QuickReorder's <input type=number> (QuickReorder.jsx:73) has no max, and rowQty floors any value, so '1e9' adds 1,000,000,000. normalizeCart (lines.js:130) keeps fractional and huge values: a cart of {'1::diamond':2.5,'366':1e9} rendered steppers showing '2.5' and '1000000000' and a header badge '1000000002.5' that overflows the Cart button. The server rejects qty > 100000 ('Invalid quantity', migration :72), and a fractional qty fails the ::integer cast, so these carts can never be submitted, and the buyer only sees the generic failure text.

owner_question: Decide whether carts with tobacco/vape items should require sign-in as an approved buyer, or allow guest quotes that collect a tobacco license number, resale certificate number and a 21+ attestation.

location: #/quote (guest) → 'Your details' form

section: Sign-in, trade application, account & admin (signed out)
title: Auth email links take over the whole site: any recovery or error link keeps the Reset Password page on top of every route
location: Any route after opening an auth email link (e.g. /#error=access_denied&error_code=otp_expired&...) → <main> stuck on the Reset Password page
evidence: Reproduced (scratchpad/pw/vauth_01_trap.mjs). Sequence: landing → title 'Reset Password · Alabama Wholesale Inc', h2 'This link has expired or was already used'. Footer 'Candies (58)' → hash #/category/CANDIES, same title and h1. location.hash='#/contact' → same. Reload at #/contact → Contact page renders. Breadcrumb 'Home' → home renders. App.jsx:316 renders ResetPasswordPage whenever auth.recovery || auth.linkError, and nothing but ResetPasswordPage.finish() calls clearRecovery (useAuth.js:105). useAuth.js:19 turns ANY error fragment into linkError, so an expired sign-up confirmation link also shows 'Choose a new password' and the text 'Reset links work once…'. A confirmation-link failure is wrongly presented as a password reset.
fix: In src/App.jsx (~158, 188-199, 316), stop rendering ResetPasswordPage in place of <main> through `accountLinkPage = auth.recovery || !!auth.linkError`. When the page detects an auth link in the URL, clear the auth hash. Only a type=recovery link should route (once) to #/reset-password. Other link errors, such as otp_expired on a sign-up confirmation, should get their own message (resend the confirmation, or sign in) and must never be described as a reset link. Clear auth.recovery and auth.linkError when the user navigates away, when they sign out, and after the password is saved, so the header nav, header search, footer links and browser Back work normally. Reset the 'Password updated' state on Sign Out. If the user signs out in the middle of a reset, show sign-in instead of 'This link has expired'.

section: Sign-in, trade application, account & admin (signed out)
title: No way to resend the sign-up confirmation email, and no landing state after confirming
location: Auth modal 'Check your inbox' step; sign-in error for unconfirmed accounts; site root after the confirmation link
evidence: The 'sent' step (AuthModal.jsx:282-299) offers only 'Done' and 'Sign in'. There is no 'Resend email' anywhere in the code (grep for 'resend' finds nothing). Signing in before confirming returns Supabase's raw 'Email not confirmed', which describeError passes straight through with no next step. useAuth.js:18 only recognises type=recovery. A successful confirmation (#access_token=…&type=signup) lands on the home page with no message, and the applicant's pending status is never explained. Applicants who miss or lose the email can only get unstuck by calling.
fix: (1) Add resendConfirmation(email) to useAuth: supabase.auth.resend({ type: 'signup', email }). (2) On the 'sent' step, add a 'Resend confirmation email' text button that calls it with signup.email, then says 'Sent again' and disables for 60 s. (3) In handleSignin, when err.code === 'email_not_confirmed', show 'Confirm your email first — we sent a link to {email}.' with the same resend button. (4) In useAuth, parse linkParams.get('type') === 'signup' (or 'email') into a `confirmedLink` flag. In App, when it is true and the profile is loaded, open AuthModal in 'status' mode, add a 'Your email is confirmed' line, and strip the fragment with history.replaceState.

title: Admin Accounts table hides the EIN, license, resale certificate and other application details staff must verify
location: #/admin → Accounts tab table (admin only)
evidence: The application collects ein, license_no, resale_cert_no, phone, business_type, state and expected_volume (AuthModal.jsx:230-271; stored by the trigger in 20260927000000_application_fields.sql). The Accounts table only renders Business, Contact, Email, Status, Tier, Role, Documents and Actions (AdminPage.jsx:187). A trade rep pressing 'Approve' therefore cannot see the numbers they are meant to check without opening the database. Documents are also shown only while status === 'pending' (AdminPage.jsx:219), so they disappear after approval or suspension.

title: The trade application loses everything typed after one click outside the dialog or one Escape press
location: Auth modal → 'Apply for an account' form (all entry points)
evidence: Reproduced (scratchpad/pw/vauth_02_dirty.mjs). Typed name 'x', business 'Test', EIN 'abc' → clicked backdrop at (40,450) (target .overlay) → 0 .dialog elements → reopened via 'Start application' → #aw-su-name '' and #aw-su-ein ''. Typing and pressing Escape did the same. The form has 11 inputs/selects (name, business, email, phone, password, business type, EIN, state, license #, resale #, monthly volume) plus 2 optional file inputs, all held in AuthModal state (AuthModal.jsx:57-58). They are discarded when App unmounts the modal (App.jsx:350).
fix: In AuthModal, compute isDirty = mode === 'signup' && (Object.keys(EMPTY_SIGNUP).some(k => signup[k] !== EMPTY_SIGNUP[k]) || Object.values(proof).some(Boolean)). Pass a guarded close to the overlay onClick, the × button and ModalLayer's onClose: when isDirty, show window.confirm('Discard your application?') or an inline confirm bar, and ignore backdrop clicks outright. Also keep the non-password fields between openings: lift `signup` into App state, or save it to sessionStorage without the password, and restore it on reopen.

title: Admin Orders cards hide the delivery method, requested date and order total, and show 'Deliver to' on will-call orders
location: #/admin → Orders tab → each .order-card header (.order-head small)
evidence: I mocked 24 orders as admin, each with delivery 'delivery' or 'willcall', preferred_date 2026-10-01, total_units and subtotal. The first card's header reads only: '9/26/2026, 10:04:09 AM · Birmingham Northside Convenience & Tobacco Outlet LLC · Test Contact · test0@example.test · 000-000-0000 · Deliver to 100 Test Street Suite 200, Testville AL 00000'. A regex test for '$<digit>' in the header returned false, so no order total is shown. Staff never see total_units or subtotal, whether the buyer chose Will-call pickup or delivery, or the requested date. submit_quote always requires a ship-to address, so every will-call order is also labelled 'Deliver to …'. The email and phone are plain text, not mailto:/tel: links. At 390px the header is a 66px run-on paragraph. AdminPage.jsx:109-111 renders only created_at, business, contact, email, phone, ship_* and tier. o.delivery, o.preferred_date, o.total_units and o.subtotal are never read, although the select('*') at line 71 already returns them.
fix:
In OrdersTab's .order-head (AdminPage.jsx:105-116), replace the single <small> run-on with a small definition list:
- 'Method': show 'Will-call pickup' when o.delivery === 'willcall', otherwise 'Delivery to {ship_street}, {ship_city}, {ship_state} {ship_zip}'. Render the address only for delivery.
- 'Requested': new Date(o.preferred_date + 'T00:00').toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric' }), or '—'.
- 'Total': `${o.total_units} units · ${formatMoney(o.subtotal)}`, or 'Unpriced quote' when subtotal is null.
- 'Contact': the contact name, the email as <a href={`mailto:${o.email}`}> and the phone as <a href={`tel:${o.phone}`}>.
Lay it out as a 2-column grid (display:grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr))) at 12–13px, and put the status select beside the ref number.

title: The Products editor can change only name, brand, price, tag and active. It can't add, delete or duplicate a SKU, change a photo, or edit the description, variants, sell unit, department/sub-line or SKU
location: #/admin → Products tab → Edit row (and the missing 'Add product' action)
evidence: Control inventory of the Products tab at all three widths: one 'Search products' input and 200 'Edit' buttons. There is no Add/New/Import/Upload/Duplicate/Delete control (0 matches). The table has no thumbnail column (0 ), so staff can't see which photo a row uses. Clicking Edit gives five fields: Product name (text), Brand (text), Price (number), Tag (select with 4 fixed values) and Active (checkbox). Category stays read-only text ('TOBACCO / Cigars & Cigarillos'). The Save PATCH observed was /rest/v1/products?id=eq.3 with body {name, brand, price, tag, active} and nothing else (AdminPage.jsx:324). Owner task walk-through: (1) Add a new SKU: impossible from the UI. A developer must edit src/data/products.js, drop a photo into src/assets/products, run npm run images and npm run seed, run the SQL and rebuild/deploy (6+ developer steps). RLS already allows admin insert/delete (rls_policies.sql:45-47), so only the UI is missing. (2) Change a product photo: impossible. img is not editable. The only storage bucket is 'application-documents' (20260927180000_application_documents.sql:9-20); there is no product-image bucket. A bare filename resolves only if it was bundled at build time: productImage() → fromSet() returns no image in production for a file not in the build (images.js:45-47, 64-70). So even a SQL edit to a new filename shows no photo; only a full URL works. (3) Fix a description, variant list, sell unit or sub-line: impossible, although the columns exist (description and sell_unit in 20260927120000_product_copy.sql:6-7; variants jsonb; cat/sub in initial_schema.sql:71-75). (4) Mark stock as short: there is no stock/availability field. The only lever is Active = off, which removes the product from the storefront and from carts. Also, useCatalog.js:24-25 still says 'The products table has no description or sell-unit columns yet', and line 30 falls back to the static description whenever the DB value is '', so a cleared description could never be saved as empty.

owner_question: Confirm how quotes should work: should staff price and answer guest quotes and convert them to orders, and should orders go through 'quoted' and 'confirmed' stages before picking?
title: A guest quote can't be priced, answered, edited or turned into an order, and orders have no quoted or confirmed stage
location: #/admin → Orders tab → order card (guest quote ALW-Q-41207 vs approved-buyer order ALW-Q-51002)
evidence:
The guest quote card offers exactly one control, 'SELECT: Status for ALW-Q-41207', with options new / contacted / fulfilled / cancelled.
- All 3 lines show '—' (unit_price null) and there is no total.
- There is no price input and no 'Send quote', 'Convert to order', 'Link to account' or 'Add line' action.
- Email and phone are plain text (0 mailto:, 0 tel: links), so staff must copy them into another app to reply.
- Guest quotes and account orders use the same header (background rgb(246,243,238), same border). The only difference is a trailing 'tier: silver' on account orders; there is no 'Guest quote' label.
- Priced cards show only line totals ($469.20), never the unit price.

The database blocks this as well:
- order_items has only a SELECT policy (rls_policies.sql:78-84). The insert policy was dropped and INSERT revoked (launch_order_boundaries.sql:258-262), and there is no update/delete policy, so admins cannot change a quantity or remove a line (task 8: short stock).
- The order_items_price trigger also fires BEFORE UPDATE OF unit_price/qty (launch_order_boundaries.sql:119-123). It sets new.unit_price := null whenever orders.user_id is null (lines 105-113), so a staff-entered price on a guest quote would be wiped. It also raises 'Product is not available' when touching a line whose product was deactivated (lines 67-70).
- orders.status allows only new/contacted/fulfilled/cancelled (initial_schema.sql:114,120; AdminPage.jsx:14). There is no quoted, confirmed, ready-for-pickup, out-for-delivery or invoiced state, and customers see the same four labels (AccountPage.jsx:16-21).
- Staff can't create an order for a customer who phones it in.

The 2026-09-25 audit (#8) asked to 'distinguish quote requested, accepted order, and scheduled delivery'. That is still not possible.

title: Nicotine warning is non-standard, 11px, only below the footer, and missing on nicotine product pages
location: Footer .fda-note on every route; vape/pouch product pages (e.g. #/product/61, #/product/60); home New arrivals rail
evidence: The only nicotine warning is the footer strip (App.jsx:1350). It is 11px text rgb(203,184,236) on rgb(28,14,64), and on #/product/61 (Geek Bar Pulse X 25K) it starts at y=2076 of a 2171px page. Nothing near vape, ZYN/PIK pouch or cigarette product content carries a warning, and the homepage's first product rail opens with 3 disposable vapes. The wording 'Tobacco products sold by Alabama Wholesale Inc. contain nicotine…' is not FDA's required statement 'WARNING: This product contains nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical.'. Under 21 CFR part 1143, ads for covered products must put that statement in the upper portion of the ad, covering at least 20% of it. The text ends 'Not for sale to minors.', which contradicts the federal 21+ minimum the site states everywhere else.
fix: Use the exact FDA-required statement ('WARNING: This product contains nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical.') in place of the reworded .fda-note text, and say 'under 21', not 'minors'. Set it at a legible size (at least 12-14px, meeting the FDA's required proportion of the ad area where applicable). Show it on every nicotine/tobacco PDP and card (Geek Bar, Foger, RAZ, ZYN, Black & Mild; App.jsx:1094), on the hero vape slide, and in the footer (App.jsx:1349-1350, index.css:428).

also_seen.location: #/ → footer .fda-note; hero slide 2; Geek Bar, Foger and RAZ cards
also_seen.evidence: The only nicotine warning is the 11px .fda-note at the very end of the page (y≈5153 of 5248 at 1440). It uses custom wording: 'WARNING: Tobacco products sold by Alabama Wholesale Inc. contain nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical…' (src/App.jsx:1350). Meanwhile the page promotes e-cigarettes: hero slide 2 is a Geek Bar Pulse X ad (hero_vape.jpg), and the New arrivals and Bestsellers rows show Geek Bar, Foger and RAZ disposables, none with a warning nearby. 21 CFR 1143.3 requires ads for covered tobacco products to carry the exact statement 'WARNING: This product contains nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical.' in the upper portion, occupying at least 20% of the ad area. Flavoured Geek Bar disposables also have no FDA marketing authorisation and have been targeted by FDA enforcement.

also_seen.location: Footer → dark warning bar (.fda-note)
also_seen.evidence: The only nicotine warning on the site is the last element on the page: 'WARNING: Tobacco products sold by Alabama Wholesale Inc. contain nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical. Products are distributed exclusively…', set in 11px #cbb8ec on #1c0e40 (contrast 9.78, so colour is fine). The FDA required statement is 'WARNING: This product contains nicotine. Nicotine is an addictive chemical.' (21 CFR 1143.3). The site paraphrases it and it is not shown on the vape, cigar or nicotine-pouch category and product pages. This is a compliance risk; counsel should confirm which placements a trade-only catalog needs.

owner_question: Provide or approve (ideally with counsel) the privacy policy details: service providers used, data sharing, retention periods for uploaded license/EIN documents, and the contact method for access/deletion requests.
title: Privacy policy omits uploaded license documents, browser storage, service providers, retention, sharing and user rights
location: #/privacy
evidence: Live #/privacy at 1440 wide shows these H2s: 'What we collect', 'Why we collect it', 'Contact the trade desk', then the ContactStrip 'Talk to the warehouse'. The support-note reads 'Last updated September 2026. Questions about this policy? Call (205) 354-4473 or email …', directly below the 'Questions about what we collect: call …' section. The policy never mentions uploaded license or resale-certificate files (private bucket 'application-documents': PDF, JPEG, PNG or HEIC, up to 10 MB, per supabase/migrations/20260927180000_application_documents.sql:9-20). It also never mentions browser storage: aw-age-verified, aw-cart, and the Supabase session token under key 'aw-auth' (src/lib/supabase.js:13-15). It names no processors (Supabase, Netlify) and says nothing about sharing, retention, security or access/deletion requests. The only date is the month-level 'September 2026' (PolicyPage.jsx:9).
fix: Expand #/privacy (PolicyPage.jsx:37-59) to cover uploaded license/EIN documents, processors (Supabase, Netlify, email provider), sharing, retention periods, browser storage (localStorage age gate/cart), and access/deletion rights with a contact method. Update the date.

also_seen.location: #/privacy → policy body
also_seen.evidence: Verified at 1440 (evidence/vsupport/privacy-1440-body.png). The documents gap is real: supabase/migrations/20260927180000_application_documents.sql creates the private bucket 'application-documents' (line 11; 10 MB limit, PDF/JPEG/PNG/HEIC) and lets admins read every file (lines 78-86, public.is_admin()). Two corrections. (1) The Netlify form definitions in index.html:62-91 are dead markup: no code in src posts to them (grep finds no 'form-name' or netlify reference), so applications go only to Supabase auth and profiles (useAuth.js:71) and documents only to Supabase storage. (2) The browser storage keys actually used are 'aw-age-verified' and 'aw-cart' (App.jsx:146, 148, 225, 265) and the Supabase session key 'aw-auth' (src/lib/supabase.js:15). 'aw-welcome-seen' is defined in content.js:107 but never read or written.

also_seen.location: #/privacy → 'What we collect' / 'Why we collect it'
also_seen.evidence: The Privacy page lists application fields and order details only (PolicyPage.jsx:43-54). It does not mention: uploaded images/PDFs of the state tobacco license and resale certificate (stored in Supabase Storage); that account, application and order data are stored with Supabase and the site is hosted by Netlify; how long applications, documents and declined applicants' data are kept, and how to request deletion; or that the site stores the session token ('aw-auth'), cart ('aw-cart') and age confirmation ('aw-age-verified') in browser localStorage. The site collects federal EINs and license scans, so these omissions are a compliance gap.

title: Re-running the product seed silently overwrites admin edits to name, brand, price and tag
location: scripts/build-seed.mjs → supabase/seed/products.sql upsert; #/admin Products editor
evidence: UPDATED = every column except id and active (build-seed.mjs:20). The generated SQL ends with `on conflict (id) do update set name = excluded.name, brand = …, tag = …, price = …`. The admin editor saves exactly those fields: name, brand, price, tag, active (AdminPage.jsx:324). BACKEND.md:30-31 tells the owner to re-run `npm run seed` and re-apply the file whenever the catalog changes, for example after adding photos. Any real prices or names entered in #/admin would revert to the products.js placeholder values. Only `active` survives.
fix: Change the product seed upsert (scripts/build-seed.mjs:20, 86-87; supabase/seed/products.sql ON CONFLICT) to insert-only (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), or to update only non-admin-managed columns, so re-running it doesn't overwrite admin edits to name, brand, price and tag. Document this in BACKEND.md.

also_seen.location: supabase/seed/products.sql (ON CONFLICT clause); BACKEND.md §2
also_seen.evidence: scripts/build-seed.mjs:20 builds UPDATED from every column except id and active. products.sql:375-387 therefore runs `on conflict (id) do update set name, brand, cat, sub, sku, flavors, variants, img, tag, price, description, sell_unit = excluded.*`. BACKEND.md:30-34 tells the owner to 're-run it and re-apply the file whenever the catalog changes' and claims 're-applying is safe'. Only `active` survives. Any price, name, brand or tag changed in Admin → Products is silently reverted to src/data/products.js on the next reseed, so there are still two sources of truth.

title: Page changes don't reset scroll correctly: the new page renders at the old scroll position and then smooth-scrolls up, and in Safari/WebKit it lands at the footer
location: All in-app navigation from a scrolled position: product cards on #/category/*, the home rails, footer links, the cart drawer's quote button. Affects Safari/WebKit on iPhone and Mac.
viewports: WebKit 390x844 (touch, DPR 3) and 1440x900; Chromium not affected
evidence: Playwright WebKit 390x844 touch DPR3: #/category/TOBACCO scrolled to y=6000 (max 14363), tapping a card goes to #/product/86 with final scrollY 2737 of max 2737. The H1 is at -2032px and only the footer is visible. Chromium gives scrollY 0. From the bottom of #/category/TOBACCO, footer 'Privacy' → #/privacy 2057/2057, 'Contact & visit' → #/contact 2810/2810, 'Trade terms' → #/terms 2991/2991 (Chromium: 0 for all). WebKit 1440x900: card from y=6000 → #/product/238 at 1271/1271 (H1 at -847px), and footer links stick at the page maximum (899, 1025, 1583). Adding html{scroll-behavior:auto!important}, or reducedMotion:'reduce' (which triggers the existing rule at src/index.css:609-610), gives y=0. The stuck position happens only when the old scrollY is greater than the new page's maximum scroll. Evidence: screenshots/qgap1wt__webkit-phone-card-landing.jpg, webkit-phone-footer-privacy-landing.png, webkit-desk-card-landing.png. Chromium equivalents are chromium-*.png in the same folder. also_seen.evidence: index.css:46 sets html { scroll-behavior: smooth }, and navigate() calls window.scrollTo(0, 0) (App.jsx:210), which inherits smooth behaviour. Clicking the footer 'Contact & visit' from the bottom of home (scrollY 4446): the new Contact page first paints showing its footer, then scrollY samples every 50 ms were 1088, 876, 496, 295, 182, 110, 51, 24, 8, 1, 0. title: Browsers that force dark mode auto-darken the whole site because it declares no color scheme and has no dark theme
location: All routes → document <head> (index.html) and :root (src/index.css). Seen in Chromium force-dark, which is the engine behind Chrome Android 'Darken websites'/auto-dark and Opera/Brave force-dark. Samsung Internet applies similar forced darkening when the phone is in dark mode.
evidence:
Chromium launched with --enable-features=WebContentsForceDark --blink-settings=forceDarkModeEnabled=true and colorScheme 'dark' (my scripts qa-gap2fd-01/06/07.mjs).
- Baseline (all routes): the page paints #121212 at DPR 1 (#101010 at DPR 2), but getComputedStyle(body).backgroundColor is rgb(255,255,255). There is no meta[name=color-scheme], and :root computes color-scheme 'normal'.

Consequences measured, merged from -4 to -11:
(a) Header hamburger bars (≤850px) and the search-button magnifier: purple #281459 on #121212, about 1.2:1. At 390px only the word 'Menu' stays visible (-4).
(b) Keyboard focus ring on the #/product/162 'Add to quote' button: #281459 on #121212 = 1.19:1, vs 15.74:1 in light mode (-5). The same purple override applies to .aw-signup, .filter-toggle, .aw-category-toggle and .sub-pill.active.
(c) Variant chips on #/product/162: selected #281459 vs idle #252320, about 1.0:1 luminance difference vs 14.22:1 in light mode. Only a faint purple hue marks the selection. The active .sub-pill has the same problem (-6).
(d) Native select arrows almost vanish: #/delivery state select, #/quote 'Delivery method', 'Sort by', and the application dialog selects (-7).
(e) White-background product and hero photos, cart/search thumbnails and the logo fringe show as bright white boxes on dark tiles (-8).
(f) The 53%-white ghost-button borders ('No, exit' on the age gate, 'Email us' on the contact strip) drop to about 1.4:1 (-9).
(g) Dialog, cart drawer, search panel and mega-menu edges merge into the dimmed page (-10).
(h) Purple headings take a pink cast, cream panels turn brown, and the NEW tag sinks into the tile (-11).

Opt-out verification (same force-dark browser, HTML patched at runtime):
- meta content="only light" → viewport paints #ffffff at 390 and 1440.
- CSS :root{color-scheme:only light} → #ffffff, with computed color-scheme 'light only'.
- meta content="light" → still #121212.

Screenshots: evidence/qa-gap2fd/fd-390-home.png, meta-onlylight-390-home.png, meta-light-390-home.png, css-onlylight-390-home.png, FD-chips.png, FD-delivery-select.png (under scratchpad).
fix:
1) index.html: on a new line directly after line 5 (the viewport meta), add `<meta name="color-scheme" content="only light" />`. It must be in the static HTML so it applies from first paint.
2) src/index.css line 9: add `color-scheme: only light;` as the first declaration inside `:root {`.
3) Keep the explicit `body { background: #fff }` at src/index.css:47.
4) Retest on a real Samsung Galaxy with Samsung Internet dark mode on. Samsung uses its own darkening algorithm, and support for the opt-out has not been verified there.
5) Do this only if Samsung Internet still darkens the page. Ship a real dark theme instead of the opt-out:
- Change the meta to content="light dark" and set `:root{color-scheme: light dark}`.
- Inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { --ink:#f1edf5; --muted:#b3acb9; --paper:#1d1a22; --cream:#2a2320; --line:#4a4452; --purple:#b9a6ec; --orange-dark:#ff8a57; --focus-ring:#ffcdb5; } }`, replace the hard-coded #fff/white/#f8f6f2 backgrounds with tokens. Affected rules: body (47), .aw-header (86), .aw-mega-menu (126), .aw-search-results (148), .home-carousel-stage (178), .sub-pill (262), .dialog (435), .drawer (456) and .form-grid fields (445).
- In the same media block:
  - Keep photo plates white: `.card-block, .pd-media, .drawer-line .thumb, .sr-thumb, .home-carousel-stage { background:#fff }`.
  - Give selected states a light fill: `.variant-chips button[aria-pressed="true"], .sub-pill.active { background:#b9a6ec; color:#1b1030 }`.
  - Give floating surfaces an edge: `.dialog, .drawer, .aw-search-results, .aw-mega-menu { background:#1d1a24; border:1px solid #5a5462 }`.
  - Make ghost borders opaque: `.age-gate .button.ghost, .contact-strip .button.ghost { border-color:#a99bd0 }`.
  - Other fixes: `.card-tag.new { background:#6a4fc0 }` and `.editorial-card.cream img.bg { mix-blend-mode:normal; opacity:.18 }`.
  - Replace the CSS-drawn icons (index.css:95-96, 273-274, 529-530; App.jsx:453, 464, 974) with inline SVG using stroke="currentColor".

title: With Google Translate on, common catalog, policy and reorder actions crash React and blank the whole site
location:
Chrome 'Translate this page' active →
- #/category/<DEPT>/<Sub line>: 'All (n)' pill, or removing the sub-line chip
- #/category/* phone Filter & Sort drawer when results reach exactly 1
- #/privacy ↔ #/shipping via the 'Customer policies' side-nav or the footer
- #/account Quick Reorder: clear the Qty field, then retype it
evidence:
Simulated Chrome Translate: every text node under #root and the portals was replaced with <font><font>…</font></font>, which detaches the original nodes, and a MutationObserver translated new content, as Translate does. Reproduced crashes:
1) #/category/TOBACCO → 'Cigarettes' pill → 'Cigars & Cigarillos' pill → 'All (68)'. Result: NotFoundError "Failed to execute 'removeChild' on 'Node'", React "The above error occurred in the <Text> component at p … at CategoryPage", #root childElementCount 0, white page.
2) 390 #/category/CANDIES → 'Bags' pill → remove the 'Bags ×' chip → same removeChild crash.
3) 390 #/category/TOBACCO → Filter & Sort → type 'kite' in 'Search in Tobacco' (1 result) → crash. App.jsx:1007 removes the 's' of 'items'.
4) #/privacy → side-nav 'Delivery' → removeChild crash. #/shipping → 'Privacy' → "Failed to execute 'insertBefore'" crash. Cause: PolicyPage.jsx:128 conditional 'Last updated …' text.
5) #/account Quick Reorder (local mocked approved session): SKU 'AW-KITE' → clear Qty → type 5 → crash. Cause: QuickReorder.jsx:79 ' · Enter a quantity of 1 or more'.
Root cause: a conditional bare string sits next to sibling nodes, so React removes or inserts a text node that Translate has already detached: App.jsx:915 `{activeSub ? ` in ${activeSub}` : ''}`, App.jsx:1007 `item{…? '' : 's'}`, PolicyPage.jsx:128, QuickReorder.jsx:78-79 and 124-125. The same pattern exists, untested, in AccountPage.jsx:134-135 and 159-162. With no error boundary the whole site goes blank (links to the known '[code] No error boundary' finding).
fix: Rule: any string that can appear, disappear or change must be the ONLY child of an element that is always rendered. 1) Rewrite each call site: - App.jsx:915 → `Showing {items.length} {`of ${inCategory.length} item${inCategory.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}${activeSub ? ` in ${activeSub}` : ''}`}` - App.jsx:1007 → `{`Show ${items.length} item${items.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}`} ↗` - PolicyPage.jsx:128 → `{policy.updated ? `Last updated ${UPDATED}. ` : ''}Questions about this policy? Call or email .` - QuickReorder.jsx:78 → `{`${res.product.name}${res.variant ? ` — ${res.variant}` : ''}`}` - QuickReorder.jsx:79 → `{`${variantSku(res.product.sku, res.variant)} · ${res.product.brand}${rowQty(row) > 0 ? '' : ' · Enter a quantity of 1 or more'}`}` - QuickReorder.jsx:124-125, AccountPage.jsx:134-135 and 159-162, and AuthModal.jsx:181-182: build one template string and render it as the sole child of a . 2) Add a safety net in src/main.jsx, before `ReactDOM.createRoot(...)` (line 6), so any missed spot degrades to stale text instead of a white page. This is the widely used guard from facebook/react#11538: `if (typeof Node === 'function' && Node.prototype) { const rc = Node.prototype.removeChild; Node.prototype.removeChild = function (child) { if (child.parentNode !== this) return child; return rc.apply(this, arguments); }; const ib = Node.prototype.insertBefore; Node.prototype.insertBefore = function (node, ref) { if (ref && ref.parentNode !== this) return node; return ib.apply(this, arguments); }; }` 3) Also wrap in an ErrorBoundary that shows a 'Something went wrong – Reload' panel (see the known error-boundary finding).

title: Keyboard focus ring is invisible on the age-gate buttons and on the purple contact strip
location: Age gate (first visit, every route): 'Yes, I am 21+' and 'No, exit'. Also the purple 'Talk to the warehouse' / 'Apply with a trade rep' contact strip at the bottom of #/apply, #/delivery, #/shipping, #/privacy and #/terms: 'Call (205) 354-4473', 'Email us' and 'Contact & visit'
evidence: Measured on the focused elements at 1440x900. Both age-gate buttons get outline 3px rgb(40,20,89) with a 3px offset, drawn on the .age-gate background rgb(40,20,89), which is 1.00:1, so the ring cannot be seen. The 'No, exit' ghost button looks exactly the same focused and unfocused (screenshots). On #/apply the contact strip has the same problem: the 'Call' .button and the 'Email us' ghost get a purple ring on purple (1.00:1), and the 'Contact & visit' text-link gets #b8390a on #281459 (2.72:1, below 3:1). Cause: index.css:59 forces `.button:focus-visible { outline-color: var(--purple) }`, which overrides the light #ffcdb5 ring set for purple surfaces at :58, and .contact-strip is missing from that list. title: SPA page changes drop keyboard focus to <body> or leave it in the header, and the new page is never announced
location: Every in-app navigation (product cards, search results, breadcrumbs, footer, mega menu, cart drawer → quote)
evidence: Keyboard journey at 1440x900: type 'backwoods' in the header search, Tab to the first result and press Enter. The URL becomes #/product/11 and document.activeElement is BODY. The next Tab lands on the header 'Sign In', so the user has to Tab through Sign Up, Cart, Categories, New Arrivals, Bestsellers, Exotics, Quick Reorder and Help again before reaching the product. Cart drawer → 'Request quote' goes to #/quote, but ModalLayer's restoreFocus puts focus back on the header 'Cart, 1 items' button, and the next Tab goes to 'Categories'. document.title does update, but no live region announces the route change, so screen-reader users get no cue that the page changed. navigate() only calls pushState, setRoute and scrollTo(0,0).

Do this for product cards, search results, breadcrumbs, footer, mega menu and cart → quote, with no smooth-scroll animation (App.jsx:197, 207-215).

title: All internal navigation is <button> + hash routing, so there are no real links and only one crawlable URL
location: Header nav, mega menu, search results, product/department cards, breadcrumbs, footer, catalog index, policy side-nav
evidence: Counted in the DOM: #/ has 0 internal <a href> and 97 <button>; #/category/TOBACCO has 0 links and 246 buttons; #/product/11 has 0 links and 60 buttons (the only anchors are tel: and mailto:). title: Cart changes in one tab overwrite another tab's cart: lines vanish silently and cleared carts come back
location: All routes → header Cart badge, cart drawer and #/quote, with the site open in two or more tabs or windows
evidence:
Script pw/gap1s-01-cart.mjs, two tabs in one browser:
(1) Tab 1 on #/product/14 (Kite) clicks 'Add to quote', giving aw-cart {"14":1}.
(2) Tab 2 on #/product/115 (Dove), opened earlier, clicks 'Add to quote', giving aw-cart {"115::original":1}. The Kite line is gone.
(3) Tab 1 still shows badge 1 and its drawer lists only 'Kite cigarette tobacco', although Dove is now the only line in storage.
(4) Tab 1 adds again, giving {"14":2}. Dove is now lost. After reloading, tab 2 shows badge 2 with Kite only.

Script gap1s-11-clear.mjs:
- Tab A on #/quote clicks 'Clear all items', giving aw-cart {}. Tab B still shows badge 8.
- Tab B adds Pure Guard 5W-30, giving {"14":5,"115::original":3,"57::5w-30":1}. The cleared cart is back.
- Reloading #/quote in tab A lists all three lines. The same thing happens after 'Back to home' clears a submitted order, so a duplicate order becomes possible.

Stale-catalog angle, script gap1s-08-stale.mjs:
- Tab B loads a catalog in which the Swisher 'Diamond' variant was renamed. normalizeCart drops the line and writes {}.
- The older tab A still shows the line. On its next add it writes {"14":1,"1::diamond":1} back, and the drawer shows 'Swisher Sweets cigarillos — Diamond'. Reloading B drops the line again, so it flickers depending on which tab wrote last.
- A quote submitted from any tab sends only that tab's in-memory lines.

Cause: the cart is read once at mount (App.jsx:148). Every mutation writes that tab's whole in-memory object back (the effect at App.jsx:225). There is no 'storage' listener anywhere in src (grep).
fix:
In src/App.jsx:
1) Delete the blanket write effect at line 225.
2) After line 231, define a write-through helper that runs OUTSIDE any setState updater (StrictMode runs updaters twice in dev):
const updateCart = (fn) => { const base = normalizeCart(safeReadJson(STORAGE.cart, {}), products); const next = fn(base); safeWriteJson(STORAGE.cart, next); setCart(next); };
3) Change addLine (244), addLines (249-259), decLine (261), removeLine (262) and clearCart (263) to call updateCart(c => …), keeping the bodies they pass to setCart today.
4) Replace the normalize effect (229-231) with:
useEffect(() => { const next = normalizeCart(safeReadJson(STORAGE.cart, {}), products); setCart(next); safeWriteJson(STORAGE.cart, next); }, [products]);
5) Add a sync effect:
useEffect(() => { const sync = () => setCart(normalizeCart(safeReadJson(STORAGE.cart, {}), products)); const onStorage = (e) => { if (e.storageArea === window.localStorage && (e.key === STORAGE.cart || e.key === null)) sync(); }; const onVis = () => { if (document.visibilityState === 'visible') sync(); }; window.addEventListener('storage', onStorage); document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', onVis); return () => { window.removeEventListener('storage', onStorage); document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', onVis); }; }, [products]);

Acceptance test:
- With two tabs open, add a different product in each. localStorage holds both lines, and both badges show 2 without a reload.
- 'Clear all items' in one tab sets the other tab's badge to 0 right away.
- A single click on 'Add to quote' in dev adds exactly 1.

title: If Sign Out can't reach Supabase, the session stays saved: the header says signed out, but a reload signs the previous buyer back in, and other tabs stay signed in
location: Header 'Sign Out' (desktop) and Menu → Account → 'Sign Out' (mobile), on any route
evidence:
Script pw/gap1s-03-signout.mjs, with a mocked approved session and the POST /auth/v1/logout?scope=global aborted, as on flaky store Wi-Fi, a captive portal or a Supabase outage:
- After clicking Sign Out, the header shows 'Sign In or Sign Up' and the page goes to #/.
- localStorage 'aw-auth' (the full session with refresh token) is still present.
- page.reload() shows 'Test Market LLC · Sign Out' again, so the next person on the shared computer is signed in as the previous buyer.

Script gap1s-04-multitab-signout.mjs (abort case), admin profile: after Sign Out in a third tab, a tab on #/account still shows 'Test Market LLC… Role Admin', and a tab on #/admin still shows the Orders / Accounts / Products admin UI. With a successful (204) logout, the same tabs correctly switch to signed out.

Cause:
- auth-js _signOut returns {error} and skips _removeSession when the logout request fails with anything other than 401/403/404 (node_modules/@supabase/auth-js/dist/module/GoTrueClient.js:3188-3196).
- useAuth.signOut ignores that result and only calls setProfile(null). The session state and storage stay as they were.
- handleLogout then navigates home as if sign-out worked.
fix:
Rewrite signOut in src/lib/useAuth.js:84-88:
const signOut = useCallback(async () => { if (!supabase) return { ok: true }; const { error } = await supabase.auth.signOut({ scope: 'local' }); if (error) { try { localStorage.removeItem('aw-auth'); localStorage.removeItem('aw-auth-code-verifier'); } catch {} } setSession(null); setProfile(null); setProfileFor(null); return { ok: !error }; }, []);

In the same hook, add a window 'storage' listener: when e.key === 'aw-auth' and e.newValue === null, call setSession(null) and setProfile(null). Other tabs then sign out even when there is no broadcast.

In App.jsx:266, make handleLogout await the result. If !ok, still navigate home and show a notice: 'Signed out on this computer. We couldn't reach the server, so other devices may still be signed in.'

title: When the session ends, the site silently switches to guest mode: mid-checkout, 'Submit order' becomes an unpriced guest 'Submit quote request' with no message
location: #/quote (also #/account, cart drawer, all price displays) when the refresh token is revoked or the token endpoint can't be reached
evidence:
Script pw/gap1s-06-midexpiry.mjs. An approved silver buyer's session expires in 125 s, and the token refresh returns 400 invalid_grant (what Supabase returns once the refresh token has been revoked, for example after a global Sign Out on another device; see the scope=global finding).

At t=0 on #/quote (prefilled):
- eyebrow 'CHECKOUT', H1 'Place your order'
- total '20 units | $823.27'
- button 'Submit order ↗'

About 30 s later, with no user action:
- header 'Sign In or Sign Up'
- eyebrow 'QUOTE REQUEST', H1 'Request your quote'
- total 'Pricing after sign-in'
- button 'Submit quote request ↗'
- no role=alert or role=status message; the form fields stay filled

A submit now runs submit_quote without a JWT:
- enforce_order_header sets user_id := auth.uid() = null.
- enforce_order_item_price leaves unit_price null for non-account orders.
- The order therefore never appears in #/account history and has no prices.

Offline variant, script gap1s-05-expiry.mjs (expired session, token endpoint unreachable):
- #/account shows 'Sign in to view your account…' although 'aw-auth' is still stored and the session is recoverable.
- 7 refresh attempts in 13 s, each logging console.error 'TypeError: Failed to fetch'.
- Nothing tells the buyer the server is unreachable.

With 400: 'aw-auth' is removed, and one 'AuthApiError: Invalid Refresh Token' is logged. No stale signed-in UI, loop or page error was observed.
fix:
1) In useAuth (lines 33-44): - Keep a ref userSignOutRef, set to true inside signOut(). - In onAuthStateChange, if event === 'SIGNED_OUT' and a session existed and userSignOutRef.current is false, setSessionEnded(true). Export sessionEnded and clearSessionEnded. - In the getSession().then handler, if the returned error is an AuthRetryableFetchError, setConnectionProblem(true) instead of treating the user as signed out. 2) In App, render a dismissible banner below the header when sessionEnded is true: 'Your session ended. Sign in again to see your account pricing. Your cart is still here.' Its [Sign in] button calls openSignin. Show a separate banner when connectionProblem is true: 'Can't reach the account service — retrying.' 3) In QuotePage, add const wasApproved = useRef(isApprovedBuyer). If wasApproved.current && !isApprovedBuyer: - Show

You were signed out. Sign in again to place this as an order.

above the submit button. - Disable the submit (line 1296) until the buyer signs in again, or clicks an explicit 'Send as a guest quote instead' link that sets wasApproved.current = false.

title: Quote reference numbers are a 5-digit client-side random value, so they collide and can be pre-claimed to block every quote
location: #/quote → Submit quote request / Submit order
evidence: App.jsx:1173 sets `useState(`ALW-Q-${Math.floor(Math.random() * 90000) + 10000}`)`, which allows only 90,000 values. submit_quote inserts p_ref_num as-is into orders.ref_num, which is `text unique not null`. Any unique_violation is re-raised as 'This quote was already submitted' (launch_order_boundaries.sql:249-251). A new quote collides with probability N/90,000 when N quotes exist, and there is a 39% chance that at least one of the first 300 quotes collides. Because refNum is fixed for the life of the page, every retry reuses the same colliding value and fails. The customer sees only the generic 'We couldn't save this quote. Please call … and reference ALW-Q-xxxxx', which names a reference belonging to someone else's order. submit_quote is granted to anon, so a script can also claim all 90,000 references and block every future quote site-wide.
fix: Generate quote reference numbers server-side in submit_quote (a sequence or long random id with a unique constraint), return the ref to the client, and stop passing a client-chosen 5-digit p_ref_num (App.jsx:1173, 1199-1202; orders.js:14).

also_seen.location: #/quote submit → submit_quote(p_ref_num)
also_seen.evidence: refNum = `ALW-Q-${Math.floor(Math.random()*90000)+10000}` (App.jsx:1173): 90,000 values. orders.ref_num is UNIQUE (initial_schema.sql:105) and submit_quote inserts the client value (launch_order_boundaries.sql:199-203). By the birthday bound, collisions become likely after a few hundred orders (~50% at ~350). A collision raises 'This quote was already submitted' (line 249-251). The client then shows 'We couldn't save this quote. Please call … and reference ALW-Q-xxxxx' (App.jsx:1202), naming a reference that belongs to a different customer's order. Approved-buyer orders also get the 'ALW-Q' (quote) prefix.

also_seen.location: #/quote → submit (submit_quote RPC)
also_seen.evidence: refNum = `ALW-Q-${Math.floor(Math.random()*90000)+10000}` (App.jsx:1173), which allows only 90,000 values. It is sent as p_ref_num (orders.js:14) into a UNIQUE column (initial_schema.sql:105). A collision raises 'This quote was already submitted' (launch migration :250-251). By the birthday bound a collision is likely once a few hundred orders exist, and each new order already has about n/90,000 odds. Because refNum is held in useState for the page's lifetime, every retry reuses the same colliding value and fails. The error then tells the buyer to 'call … and reference ALW-Q-xxxxx' (App.jsx:1202), a number that exists nowhere in the system (or belongs to someone else's order).

owner_question: Set up an SMTP provider (Resend, Postmark or SES) with a sender address on your business domain and SPF/DKIM records, then enter it in the Supabase Auth settings along with the production and deploy-preview redirect URLs.
title: Backend setup never configures a production email sender, so confirmation and password-reset emails will not reach customers
location: Apply for a trade account → 'Check your inbox'; Sign in → Forgot password? → 'Check your inbox'
evidence: The signup flow depends on the confirmation email (AuthModal.jsx:173, 286), and password reset depends on the reset email (useAuth.js:93-97). BACKEND.md covers env vars, Site URL and the redirect allow-list, but never covers custom SMTP, sender domain (SPF/DKIM), auth rate limits or email templates. It even suggests turning confirmation off (BACKEND.md:80-83). Supabase's built-in sender only delivers to members of the project's team ('Email address not authorized' for everyone else) and is limited to about 2 messages per hour (https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-smtp). If the project still uses the default sender, real applicants never get a confirmation link and resets never arrive. The UI still says the email is on its way. signUp also passes no `emailRedirectTo`, so confirmation links always go to the Site URL. The dashboard settings could not be inspected in this review.
fix: Add a 'Production email' section to BACKEND.md. Steps: configure custom SMTP (Resend, Postmark or SES) under Authentication → Emails → SMTP Settings, with a sender on the business domain and SPF/DKIM records. Raise 'Rate limit for sending emails' under Authentication → Rate Limits to a sensible value (e.g. 100/hour). Keep 'Confirm email' ON in production and state that it must not be disabled outside a test project. Customise the Confirm signup and Reset password templates with the business name. In src/lib/useAuth.js signUp, add `emailRedirectTo: `${window.location.origin}/`` inside `options`, and add the production and deploy-preview origins to the redirect allow-list.

location: index.html <head> (canonical, og:url, og:image, twitter:image, JSON-LD); /robots.txt; /sitemap.xml; BACKEND.md Supabase Auth 'Site URL' step
evidence: Checked 2026-09-28. `dig alabamawholesaleinc.com A` and `dig www.alabamawholesaleinc.com A` both return NXDOMAIN, and `whois -h whois.verisign-grs.com alabamawholesaleinc.com` returns 'No match'. fix: (1) Before launch, register alabamawholesaleinc.com (or decide the final domain) and add it in Netlify → Domain management as the primary domain with HTTPS. title: A production build without the Supabase env vars succeeds silently and ships a site with sign-in, applications and quotes disabled
location: Netlify production build → every route (auth dialog, #/quote submit, #/account, #/admin)
evidence: src/lib/supabase.js:7-18 creates a null client when either variable is missing. src/App.jsx:1183 and :1293 then show the 'can’t be saved' message, and the submit button at :1296 is disabled. The build passes anyway: neither vite.config.js nor netlify.toml has a guard. It has happened twice. (a) The old ~/Desktop/alabamawholesaleinc.com/alabama-wholesale-netlify-source/dist (2026-05-24) has 0 'supabase.co' in assets/index-D3CurPUo.js. (b) The current worktree's dist/ (built Sep 26 22:08:58, commit bf94cca) has 0 'supabase', 'auth/v1', 'rest/v1', 'aw-auth' or 'submit_quote' strings in dist/assets/*.js, and 4 copies of the 'can’t be saved right now' fallback. Deploying it would ship a site where sign-in, applications and quotes are all disabled. Evidence: screenshots/qa-gap2-launch-lifecycle__dist-and-domain-check.txt
fix: Turn vite.config.js into a function and fail every production build that lacks the variables, not only Netlify production builds. `import { defineConfig, loadEnv } from 'vite'; export default defineConfig(({ command, mode }) => { const env = loadEnv(mode, process.cwd(), ''); if (command === 'build' && mode === 'production' && env.ALLOW_NO_BACKEND !== '1' && (!/^https:\/\/[a-z0-9-]+\.supabase\.co\/?$/.test(env.VITE_SUPABASE_URL || '') || !env.VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY)) { throw new Error('VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY must be set for production builds (set ALLOW_NO_BACKEND=1 to build a static-only preview on purpose).'); } return { /* existing config */ }; });`. Keep the CI workflow's dummy-value build working by passing ALLOW_NO_BACKEND=1, or valid-looking dummy values, in that job only. Delete the stale backend-less local dist/ (`rm -rf dist`). Add a line to BACKEND.md section 4 and NETLIFY-DEPLOY.md saying the build now fails without the variables.

title: Searches with more than one word are padded with unrelated products
location: Header search dropdown
evidence:
The scorer awards `terms.filter(t => h.includes(t)).length * 8` whenever any single word matches, and keeps every product with score > 0 (App.jsx:66, :69). Observed dropdowns:
- 'geek bar' shows 10 results: the 4 Geek Bar products, then 3 Musketeers bars, Airheads bars, Almond Joy bars, Atkinson's Peanut Butter Bars jar, Butterfinger bars and Dove bar soap.
- 'red bull': the 4 Red Bull SKUs, then 24/7 cigarettes, 4K's cigarillos, 4K's Wraps, Airheads soda, Ajax dish liquid and American Club pipe tobacco (these match the variant 'Red' or other words).
- 'swisher sweets': 6 Swisher products, then Airheads, Charms Blow Pop, Cherry candy lumps and Ferrara boxes (they match 'Sweets & Gummies').
- 'white owl': 2 White Owl products, then Charcoal bags, Cheez-It, Durags and Foam bowls.
- 'ss': Bath tissue and Glass cleaner are ranked above Swisher Sweets AW-SS.
Products matching all words vs products matching any word: geek bar 4 vs 25, red bull 4 vs 52, swisher sweets 6 vs 32, white owl 2 vs 29.
fix: In getSearchMatches, first keep only products where `terms.every(t => h.includes(t))`. Better, match at word starts with `new RegExp('\\b' + escape(t))`. Score and sort only that set: name match, then SKU prefix, then brand. Give an exact SKU match (`p.sku.toLowerCase() === q`) a +200 boost. Fall back to any-word matching only when the all-words set is empty, and then label the dropdown 'No exact matches — related products'. Remove the per-term `* 8` bonus from the main path.

title: Search misses plurals, spacing variants, typos and apostrophe variants ('reese's', 'm&m's'), including the words in its own placeholder

The placeholder reads 'Search 368 SKUs — cigars, disposables, candy, drinks…' (App.jsx:460). Observed results:

Lowercase, treat curly and straight apostrophes the same and strip punctuation (’ ' & -), collapse whitespace, also match with spaces removed, apply simple singular/plural stemming, and add small typo tolerance (e.g. Fuse.js or edit distance 1). title: Client price math does not round unit prices, so 'each' × qty ≠ line total and the estimate differs from the saved subtotal
location: Cart drawer / #/quote line prices and totals for silver/gold approved buyers
evidence: priceForProfile returns an unrounded float (App.jsx:31); line totals use `it.qty * it.price` (App.jsx:1261) and cartTotal sums the same (App.jsx:238). The server rounds the unit price to cents first: `round(v_product.price * (1 - discount), 2)` (launch_order_boundaries.sql:111). Computed examples at qty 7. Silver, $45.10 list: checkout shows '$42.84 each' (JS toFixed on 42.845), line total $299.91, server $299.95. Silver, $51.51: '$48.93 each', line $342.54, but 7 × $48.93 = $342.51, which is what the server saves. Gold, $84.34: client $531.34 vs server $531.37. The client also hard-codes the discounts `{ standard: 0, silver: 0.05, gold: 0.10 }` (App.jsx:28), duplicating the pricing_tiers table, so they drift if an admin edits tiers.
fix: Round tier unit prices to cents before multiplying (Math.round(price*(1-discount)*100)/100), matching the server calculation, so each × qty equals the line total and the estimate matches the saved subtotal (App.jsx:28-32, 235-238, 1249).

title: Everything typed into the quote form is lost on navigation, including via the page's own 'Choose variant' link
location: #/quote form
evidence: I typed 'ZZ TEST' into Business and 'ZZ' into Contact, clicked the Home breadcrumb, then used browser Back to #/quote. Business came back as '' (form state lives only in QuotePage useState). The quote page itself sends users away with 'Choose variant' (App.jsx:1253) and product-name clicks, so a buyer who fixes a line loses 11 fields of details.
fix: Save a draft of `data` (excluding nothing sensitive beyond contact info) to sessionStorage key 'aw-quote-draft' on change (debounced 300 ms). Initialize from it on mount and clear it on successful submit. Wrap reads and writes in try/catch like safeReadJson. Also fixing the inline variant select (see the bare-line finding) removes the need to leave the page.

title: Checkout line cards have zero horizontal padding: thumbnails touch the left border and the × touches the right
location: #/quote → .checkout-line items
evidence: At 390px, the .checkout-line box starts at x=16 and its .thumb at x=17, flush against the 1px border. At 1440px the thumbnail sits at x=81 against the border at x=80, and the × button meets the right edge. Cause: `.checkout-line { padding: 12px }` (index.css:337) is overridden by the later equal-specificity rule `.drawer-line { padding: 12px 0 }` (index.css:463), because the <li> has both classes.
fix: Raise specificity: change index.css:337 to `.drawer-line.checkout-line { border: 1px solid var(--line); padding: 12px 16px; }`, or move the .checkout-line rule below .drawer-line.

title: 'Clear all items' empties the whole cart instantly with no confirmation or undo
location: #/quote → 'Clear all items' text link under the line list
evidence: A single click on 'Clear all items' (App.jsx:1266) set aw-cart to {} and replaced the page with 'Your cart is empty'. There is no confirm and no undo. The link sits directly below the last line's controls, where a stray tap is likely on mobile.
fix: Before clearing, keep the previous cart in a ref (`lastCleared = cart`). Show an inline banner 'Cart cleared · Undo' (role="status") for 8 seconds, with Undo calling setCart(lastCleared). Alternatively, gate the action with window.confirm('Remove all N items from this quote?'). Move the link to the right of a subtotal row, away from the steppers.

title: Cart lines are silently deleted when a product is deactivated or a variant renamed
location: App load / live catalog refresh → normalizeCart
evidence: Seeded aw-cart with '9999' (unknown product) and '1::nonexistent' (unknown variant). After reload both lines were gone from storage and the drawer, with no message. Live products are loaded `.eq('active', true)` (useCatalog.js:19), so when an admin deactivates a product, every buyer's saved line for it disappears the next time they open the site. Reorders do report 'No longer available', but normal carts do not.
fix: Don't normalize/delete cart lines until the live catalog has loaded (App.jsx:229-231; useCatalog.js:13-36). For lines whose product is deactivated or whose variant was renamed, keep them flagged as 'no longer available' with a notice and let the user remove them, instead of silently deleting (lines.js:126-148).

also_seen.location: All routes → cart normalization (App effect on products)

title: Auth and upload failures show raw Supabase error text to customers
location: Auth modal sign-in/sign-up/reset errors; upload errors; #/reset-password; #/account order-history error
evidence: describeError (AuthModal.jsx:21-25) only rewrites network errors and otherwise shows err.message verbatim. The same pattern is in documentErrorMessage (documents.js:41-46) and ResetPasswordPage.jsx:27-30. AccountPage.jsx:114 renders `Couldn't load orders: {error}` with the PostgREST message. Customers would therefore see backend strings such as 'Invalid login credentials', 'Email not confirmed', 'User already registered', 'For security purposes, you can only request this after 49 seconds', 'new row violates row-level security policy' or 'mime type image/heic-sequence is not supported'. Not triggered live, because remote writes are blocked in this review.
fix: Create src/lib/authErrors.js exporting friendlyAuthError(err, what) that switches on err.code (supabase-js v2 AuthApiError): invalid_credentials → 'That email and password don’t match. Try again or reset your password.'; email_not_confirmed → 'Confirm your email first — check your inbox or resend the link.'; user_already_exists → 'An account already uses this email. Sign in or reset your password.'; weak_password → 'Choose a stronger password: ' + err.reasons; over_email_send_rate_limit / over_request_rate_limit → 'Please wait a minute before trying again.'; any other code → the existing phone/email fallback. Use it in AuthModal, ResetPasswordPage and documents.js, and replace AccountPage.jsx:114 with 'We couldn’t load your orders. Refresh the page or call the trade desk.' Log the raw error with console.warn.

title: After sign-in the dialog closes silently if the profile is missing or slow, leaving the header looking signed out
location: Auth modal 'Signing you in…' step; header account actions
evidence: The checking effect (AuthModal.jsx:76-81) moves to 'status' only when `profile && profile.status !== 'approved'`. When the profile fetch fails (useAuth.js:56 just console.warns), the dialog calls onClose. A second effect (:82-86) also closes the dialog after 10 s with no message. section: Sign-in, trade application, account & admin (signed out)
title: Keyboard focus falls to <body> when the dialog returns to the step it opened on
location: Auth modal: Sign Up → Continue → 'Back to the checklist'; Sign In → 'No account? Apply instead' → 'Already approved? Sign in'
evidence: Measured document.activeElement. Header Sign Up → checklist (focus on Continue) → signup form (focus on #auth-title) → 'Back to the checklist' leaves focus on BODY. Sign In → Apply instead (focus on #auth-title) → 'Already approved? Sign in' also leaves focus on BODY. The effect at AuthModal.jsx:68-72 skips focusing the heading whenever mode equals the initial mode, and the button that had focus has unmounted.
fix: Replace the initialModeRef guard with a first-run ref: `const firstRun = useRef(true); useEffect(() => { if (firstRun.current) { firstRun.current = false; return; } titleRef.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true }); }, [mode]);`. Focus then moves to the heading on every step change, including returns to the first step.

location: Transactional email: 'Apply for an account' → Submit application → confirmation email; Sign in → Forgot password? → reset email
evidence: supabase/ has only migrations/ and seed/; there is no config.toml and no templates/ directory. BACKEND.md:74-83 never mentions email templates ('You'll get a confirmation email from Supabase.'). The public auth settings (GET /auth/v1/settings) show mailer_autoconfirm=false, so every applicant receives a confirmation email and signUp returns no session. src/lib/useAuth.js:67-73 calls auth.signUp without emailRedirectTo; :95 sets the reset redirect to `${origin}/`. (c) Take the phone, address and hours in the template footer from src/data/content.js COMPANY ((205) 354-4473; 613 Graymont Ave N, Birmingham, AL 35203; Mon–Fri 7:00 AM – 6:00 PM, Sat–Sun 8:00 AM – 5:30 PM), and note in BACKEND.md that the template footer must be updated whenever COMPANY changes.

title: License-document status shows 'Not uploaded' for files that are uploading or already saved (two uploads at once, or an upload made while the list is still loading)
location: #/apply (signed in, pending) → 'License documents' panel → the status line under each file input
evidence: Uploads were mocked locally with a 2.5 s delay. Repro A, two uploads: choose the license, then the resale certificate 0.3 s later. At t=1.0 s the license reads 'Not uploaded' with its input re-enabled while its upload is still running. At t=2.9 s the license has finished, but the resale reads 'Not uploaded' with its input enabled while its upload is still running. Both show correctly only at t=4.4 s. Cause: busyType is a single string (DocumentUploads.jsx:115). Picking the second file overwrites it, and the first upload's finally block sets it to null (:155). Repro B, stale list: the initial list GET is slow (3 s) and shows 'Checking…', but both inputs stay enabled. Upload the license during the check: at t=1.5 s it shows 'Uploaded on September 28, 2026 · TEST-ONLY-license.pdf'. At t=4.0 s the stale initial response lands and sets it back to 'Not uploaded', although the server row exists (1 row). Cause: the initial effect (:126-128) sets records unconditionally. A buyer who sees 'Not uploaded' re-uploads or emails the files.
fix: In ApplicationDocuments, replace `const [busyType, setBusyType] = useState(null)` with `const [busy, setBusy] = useState({})`. In onPick call `setBusy(b => ({ ...b, [type]: true }))`, and in finally (still guarded by the token) call `setBusy(b => ({ ...b, [type]: false }))`. Pass `busy` to DocumentFields instead of busyType and compute `const isBusy = !!busy?.[doc.id]` at line 54. Disable the controls until the first list has loaded: `controlsDisabled = disabled || !isBackendConfigured || loading || !userId || records == null`. Also add `const touched = useRef(false)`, set it true at the start of onPick, and in the initial list effect only apply the rows when !touched.current (or merge by keeping the newer uploaded_at per document_type).

title: After a failed upload the input still shows the failed file next to the old 'Uploaded' line, and picking the same file again does not retry
location: #/apply (signed in, pending) → 'License documents' → choose a file whose upload fails
evidence: Replacing the uploaded resale certificate with a storage upload fulfilled locally as 413 leaves three messages that contradict each other: the native input shows 'TEST-ONLY-license.pdf' (the file that failed), the status line still reads 'Uploaded on September 28, 2026 · TEST-ONLY-resale.pdf', and the error line reads 'The object exceeded the maximum allowed size'. The same happens with a 400. onChange clears event.target.value only when client validation fails (DocumentUploads.jsx:34-35), so after any upload the input keeps its file. In Chrome and Safari, choosing the same file again fires no change event, so 'You can try again' (documents.js:45) cannot work without first choosing a different file. The status line never names the file that failed. (Raw error text and the filename shown twice are known and not re-reported.)
fix: In DocumentFields onChange, read the file and then always reset the input: `const file = event.target.files?.[0] || null; event.target.value = '';` (so re-choosing the same file fires change). In ApplicationDocuments keep the last attempted File per type: `const [attempt, setAttempt] = useState({})`, set in onPick before uploading. On error, render the status line as `Couldn’t upload ${attempt[type].name}.` followed by `<button type="button" className="text-link" onClick={() => onPick(type, attempt[type], null)}>Try again</button>`, and keep the previous 'Uploaded on … · <old name>' as a second line prefixed 'Still on file:'. Clear attempt[type] on success.

title: After Submit application the confirmation step opens where the long form was scrolled, so on landscape phones 'Check your inbox', the email address and step 1 are off-screen
location: Auth dialog → application form scrolled to 'Submit application' → 'sent' ('Check your inbox') or 'status' ('Your account is pending approval') step
evidence: Scrolled the form to its submit button (as a user must), then switched the step with the React state hook. At 844x390 the form scrollTop was 905. The 'sent' step opened at scrollTop 347 with the H2 at y=-199: the first thing visible is step 2 'We review your application' and the Done button. The 'status' step opened at scrollTop 306 with the H2 at y=-158. At 1280x720 the offset is 17 px, and at 390x844 it is 9-26 px. The mode effect focuses the heading with preventScroll: true (AuthModal.jsx:69-72), so focus lands on an off-screen heading and nothing scrolls it into view. The same leftover offset affects 'reset' → 'reset-sent' (scrollTop 55 at 844x390).
fix: In the step-change effect (AuthModal.jsx:69-72) reset the dialog's scroll before focusing: `const dlg = titleRef.current?.closest('.dialog'); if (dlg) dlg.scrollTop = 0; titleRef.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true });`.

title: On the 'account on hold' sign-in step, the phone and email look like plain text, and the main button goes to a page that doesn't explain the hold
location: Auth dialog → sign in with a suspended account → 'ACCOUNT ON HOLD / Your account needs attention' step
evidence: Computed styles of the two links in '.dialog > .desc': color rgb(95,88,98), the same as the paragraph; text-decoration none; font-weight 400. The same unstyled-link rule applies to any future TradeDesk link placed in .desc.

In AuthModal.jsx status actions (314-318), when status === 'suspended', render `Call {COMPANY.phone}`, then `Email the trade desk`, then the 'Close' text-link. title: The #/apply page head, intro, contact strip and tab title are written for someone who hasn't applied, even for signed-in pending, approved or suspended accounts

evidence: For a pending account: eyebrow 'OPEN AN ACCOUNT'; H1 'Your trade account'; intro 'Here is what to have ready, and what happens after you apply.' Approved: 'Your trade account is active', with links to the catalog, My account and Quick Reorder, and no application checklist. Suspended: 'Account on hold', with what to do and the contact details. Guests keep the current 'Open an account' copy. Update the eyebrow, intro paragraph, the bottom contact-strip heading ('Apply with a trade rep') and the document title ('Apply for a Trade Account') to match each state.

owner_question: Which staff email address (or channel) should be notified when an applicant uploads license documents, and how quickly will a trade rep review them?
title: After both documents upload, the panel still says 'Optional … or send proof later': no 'received' summary, no way to open the uploaded file, and staff aren't notified
location: #/apply (signed in, pending) → status panel and 'License documents' panel after both files upload; also the dialog 'status' step after a sign-up that uploaded files
evidence: #/apply, pending profile, 1440x900, uploads mocked 200. After both files upload, only the two per-file lines change, to 'Uploaded on September 28, 2026 · QA-ONLY-license.pdf' and '… · QA-ONLY-resale.pdf' (12px, weight 400, rgb(36,32,44), no success styling). The status panel still reads 'A trade rep is reviewing your license information…'. The panel's only link is the email address; createDocumentViewUrl (documents.js:157) is used only by admin. supabase/migrations/20260927180000_application_documents.sql has no trigger or webhook on profile_documents.
fix:
In ApplicationDocuments (DocumentUploads.jsx) compute `const have = DOCUMENT_TYPES.filter(d => records?.some(r => r.document_type === d.id)).length;`. Above render

{have === 2 ? 'Both documents received. A trade rep will check them with your application; nothing else is needed.' : have === 1 ? '1 of 2 documents received.' : 'No documents yet. Uploading them now speeds up approval.'}

. In DocumentFields, when showStatus is true, omit the ' Optional' span (line 63) and replace the note at line 42 with 'Uploading a new file replaces the one on file.'. When showStatus && record, render a 'View' text-link button after the status text: onClick={async () => { const url = await createDocumentViewUrl(record.storage_path); if (url) window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener'); }}. Add CSS after index.css:803: `.doc-status[data-document-status=uploaded] { font-weight: 600; color: var(--purple); } .doc-status[data-document-status=uploaded]::before { content: '✓ '; }`. Skip the AuthModal status-step change: it's unreachable while email confirmation is on. For staff: add a Supabase Database Webhook (Dashboard → Database → Webhooks) on INSERT and UPDATE of public.profile_documents that POSTs to a new Edge Function `notify-trade-desk`, which emails the trade desk the business name and document type.
