title: Quick Reorder: 'Add N lines to order' silently does nothing when any row has quantity 0 or a decimal, and 150,000 units are accepted
location: #/account → Quick Reorder ('Reorder by SKU') form → 'Add N lines to order' button
evidence:
Signed in as a silver buyer, I tested three cases:
- Case A: row 1 AW-KITE qty 3, row 2 AW-SS-RED qty 0. The button reads 'Add 1 line to order' and is enabled. Clicking it leaves aw-cart at '{}' with no summary: form.checkValidity() is false because the qty input has min=1 ('Value must be greater than or equal to 1'), so the browser blocks the submit and only shows a native tooltip. The app's own note says '1 line needs attention before it can be added', which implies the other line will go through.
- Case B: qty 2.5 counts as ready (rowQty floors it to 2) and the row shows no warning. The button reads 'Add 2 lines to order', but step=1 validation blocks it again with no in-app message.
- Case C: qty 150000 is accepted into the cart ('1::red':150000; summary 'Added 2 lines (150003 units)'), but enforce_order_item_price rejects qty > 100000, so the buyer only finds out at checkout through a generic save error.
Also, the qty-0 hint 'Enter a quantity of 1 or more' is grey 11px small text, while other row problems are orange (.qr-problem).
fix:
In QuickReorder.jsx: 1. Add noValidate to the
(line 51) so rows needing attention never block the ready ones. 2. Replace rowQty with `const rowQty = (row) => { const n = Number(row.qty); return Number.isInteger(n) && n >= 1 && n <= 100000 ? n : 0; };` so decimals and out-of-range values count as needing attention instead of being floored. 3. Add max="100000" to the qty input (line 73). 4. For an ok match with an invalid qty, render the hint as

Enter a whole number from 1 to 100,000

instead of the grey small text on line 79. 5. Keep the enabled button's label equal to the number of lines that will actually be added.

title: Order history doesn't say what was requested, or whether each entry was a quote or an order, and uses internal status names
location: #/account → Order history → .order-card
evidence: I mocked 25 orders covering every status. Each card shows only the ref, 'the date at 10:04:09 AM' (seconds included), units, subtotal, a status pill and the lines. In AccountPage.jsx:
- Extend the select (line 34) with delivery, preferred_date, ship_street, ship_city, ship_state, ship_zip and notes.
- In each card header, show `{o.subtotal == null ? 'Quote request' : 'Order'}`, the date as toLocaleDateString('en-US', { month: 'short', day: 'numeric', year: 'numeric' }), and a second line 'Will-call pickup' or 'Delivery to …' plus 'Requested {date}'. location: #/, #/category/CANDIES, #/category/TOBACCO, related cards on #/product/* → .card-meta price (approved buyer)

title: Confirmation screen's 'ORDER RECEIVED' eyebrow and reference number are 360px off-centre on desktop

title: Quick Reorder rows waste space: three blank rows each with Remove, a ~600px gap before Remove, no prices, and 'Add another line' doesn't focus the new row
location: #/account → Quick Reorder (.qr-row, .qr-actions)
evidence:

title: Orders can't be searched, filtered by date, printed as a pick list or packing slip, exported, given an internal note, or audited for who changed what
location: #/admin → Orders tab (whole tab)
evidence: Local admin mock, 1440x900, Orders tab. Pills: 'new (3)', 'contacted (1)', 'fulfilled (1)', 'cancelled (1)', 'all (6)'. There are 0 <input>/<textarea> outside the cards and 0 buttons or links matching print|export|csv|pick|packing|invoice. Staff cannot search by ref, business, email or phone, and cannot filter by created date, preferred_date or delivery method, so there is no way to list tomorrow's route. A fulfilled order can be found only by opening the 'fulfilled' or 'all' pill and scrolling. Printing (emulateMedia print, 'all' view) gives 3 Letter pages. They include the trade bar, header and footer; status selects print as dropdowns; and there is no per-order pick list or packing slip. The only note on a card is the customer's orders.notes ('Notes: …', AdminPage.jsx:126). orders has no internal-note, assignee or event-history table (initial_schema.sql:103-122). orders_self_read (rls_policies.sql:59-60) exposes every orders column to the customer, so internal notes can't live on orders. A status change sends PATCH {status} only (AdminPage.jsx:79), and nothing records who changed what, or when. orders.updated_at is touched by a trigger (initial_schema.sql touch_orders) but is never displayed. The generic site-chrome-in-print problem is covered by the known '[design] No print stylesheet' finding. This item is about the admin-specific pick list and packing slip.
fix:
1) Add a toolbar above .order-list in OrdersTab (AdminPage.jsx:88-100):
- A search input that queries server-side with .or(`ref_num.ilike.%${q}%,business.ilike.%${q}%,email.ilike.%${q}%,phone.ilike.%${q}%,contact.ilike.%${q}%`).
- 'Placed from/to' (created_at) and 'Deliver on' (preferred_date) date inputs, plus a Delivery / Will-call select.
- Keep all of these in the hash, e.g. #/admin/orders?q=&status=&from=&to=.
2) Add per-order 'Print pick list' and 'Print packing slip' buttons that open #/admin/orders/<id>/print. That view shows lines sorted by department/sub-line with a ☐ column, SKU, qty and unit, plus ship-to, delivery method, date and customer notes.
3) Add an admin-scoped print block at the end of src/index.css: @media print { .trade-bar, .trade-only, .aw-header, footer, .sub-pills, .order-head select { display:none } .order-card { break-inside: avoid } }. The site-wide print stylesheet is tracked separately.
4) Add an 'Export CSV' button for the current filter. Columns: ref_num, created_at, business, email, delivery, preferred_date, status, sku, product_name, qty, unit_price, line_total, subtotal.
5) Migration: create public.order_admin_notes (id bigserial pk, order_id uuid references orders on delete cascade, author uuid default auth.uid(), body text not null, created_at timestamptz default now()) and public.order_events (id bigserial pk, order_id uuid references orders on delete cascade, at timestamptz default now(), actor uuid default auth.uid(), from_status text, to_status text, note text). Add an 'after update of status on public.orders' trigger that inserts into order_events. Enable RLS on both tables with admin-only policies (using/with check public.is_admin()). Add alter table public.orders add column assigned_to uuid references public.profiles(id).
6) Under each order card, render a notes box, an 'Assigned to' select and a timeline ('Contacted by Test Owner · Sep 28 9:14 AM').

title: The admin Orders list never refreshes: a new quote appears only after a tab switch or reload, and nothing marks orders that are new since the last visit
location: #/admin → Orders tab; header 'Admin' link; browser tab title
evidence:
Steps: #/admin was loaded, a new order ALW-Q-99001 was added to the (mocked) backend, window 'focus' and 'visibilitychange' were fired, and the page waited 40 s.
- Orders requests: 2 before, 2 after. The new order was not shown and the pill still read 'new (3)'.
- Only clicking Accounts then Orders re-fetched (4 GETs) and showed it.
- There is no Supabase realtime channel. The only setInterval in src is the hero carousel (App.jsx:653).
- There is no 'Refresh' button or 'Last updated' time.
- document.title stays 'Admin · Alabama Wholesale Inc' (App.jsx:109), and the header 'Admin' button (App.jsx:487) has no count.
- No card is highlighted as new since the last visit.

The missing email notification is a separate, known finding. This one is about in-app awareness.
fix:
1) In OrdersTab, subscribe with supabase.channel('admin-orders').on('postgres_changes', { event: '*', schema: 'public', table: 'orders' }, reload).subscribe(). Remove the channel on unmount. Migration: alter publication supabase_realtime add table public.orders;
2) Fall back to setInterval(reload, 60000), plus reload on document visibilitychange when visible.
3) Add a 'Refresh' mini-btn and 'Updated hh:mm' text next to the status pills.
4) Save localStorage 'aw-admin-orders-seen-at' (wrapped in try/catch) when the tab is viewed. Give cards with created_at > seenAt a 'NEW' badge and a 3px orange left border.
5) When the unseen count > 0, set document.title to `(${n}) Admin · Alabama Wholesale Inc` and show the count as a badge on the header 'Admin' button.

title: Order status (including 'cancelled') and account status/tier change the instant a dropdown value is picked: no confirmation, feedback or undo, and the order card vanishes
location: #/admin → Orders card status select; Accounts Status / Tier selects and Approve button
evidence:
Orders, on the default 'new' view: choosing 'cancelled' on ALW-Q-41207 immediately sent PATCH /rest/v1/orders?id=eq.o-guest-1 {"status":"cancelled"}.
- The card disappeared from the list at once (pills went to 'cancelled (2)').
- Keyboard focus fell to <body>.
- 0 dialogs, 0 role=status/alert messages, no Undo. Staff had to open 'cancelled' to find the order again.

Accounts:
- Status → 'suspended' sent PATCH /profiles?id=eq.u-1 {"status":"suspended"} instantly, with no reason asked.
- Tier → 'standard' sent PATCH {"pricing_tier":"standard"} instantly.
- Double-clicking 'Approve' sent 2 identical PATCH {status:'approved'} requests, because the button is not disabled while saving.

Every account change also re-signs every document URL (an extra POST /storage/v1/object/sign on each change).

Role changes are a known finding and are excluded here.
fix:
1) Cancelling an order and suspending an account open a confirm dialog: 'Cancel ALW-Q-41207 for TEST Guest Corner Store?' with a required reason <textarea>. Store the reason in order_events.note or profile admin notes (see the other findings).
2) Other transitions apply optimistically: update local state with setOrders(prev => prev.map(...)) instead of reload(), and keep the card visible in the current filter until the next refresh, with a 'Moved to contacted' tag.
3) Show a role=status toast for 8 s, e.g. 'ALW-Q-41207 marked Contacted · Undo'. Undo PATCHes the previous status.
4) Keep focus on the same select, or move it to the toast.
5) Disable the select or button while the request is in flight (a savingId state), so double-clicks send one request.
6) Don't reload documents on every profile change: split reload() so updateProfile refetches only profiles.

title: The Accounts tab has no search, no account detail page, no way to edit phone, business or address, no notes, no per-account order history and no 'Add account'
location: #/admin → Accounts tab
evidence:
Columns: Business, Contact, Email, Status, Tier, Role, Documents, Actions.
- 0 text inputs and no search box. Finding one store means scrolling the whole table.
- 0 mailto:/tel: links.
- Clicking the business name 'TEST Approved Market LLC' does nothing (hash stays #/admin, 0 dialogs, the cell is plain text).

Hidden EIN/license columns are a known finding and are excluded. profiles_self_read (rls_policies.sql:19-20) lets customers read their own profile row, so staff notes can't be stored on profiles.

title: No bulk price change, no CSV export or import, and no way to edit tier discounts: a supplier price rise means editing every row by hand
location: #/admin → Products tab
evidence:
Test case: a 5% supplier increase across Swisher Sweets. Admin search 'Swisher' finds 6 rows.
- It took 18 UI actions (Edit → type price → Save, ×6).
- That produced 6 separate PATCHes, and each Save re-downloaded the entire 368-row catalog (6 full products?select=* GETs; AdminPage.jsx:273-277).
- Only one row can be in edit mode at a time (a single `editing` object, line 265).
- The same change across the whole catalog would be 368 × 3 = 1,104 actions.

No row checkboxes or multi-select. 0 'Export'/'Import'/'CSV' controls on any admin tab.

pricing_tiers is admin-writable (rls_policies.sql:92-94) but has no admin UI, so changing Silver from 5% to 7% needs SQL. The client-side hard-coded tier values are a separate known finding.
fix:
1) Add a leading checkbox column plus 'Select all (filtered)'. When anything is selected, show a bulk bar: 'Set price', 'Adjust price by % / $' (with a preview table old → new, rounded to 0.01), 'Set tag', 'Activate', 'Deactivate'.

create function public.admin_bulk_price(p_ids int[], p_pct numeric default 0, p_amount numeric default 0) returns int language plpgsql security definer set search_path=public as $$ begin if not public.is_admin() then raise exception 'admin only'; end if; update public.products set price = round(price*(1+p_pct/100)+p_amount,2) where id = any(p_ids); return (select count(*) from public.products where id = any(p_ids)); end $$;

title: The admin product editor has no validation: it saves a blank name or brand and negative or absurd prices, and a cleared price becomes NaN and is sent as null
location: #/admin → Products → Edit row (name, brand, price inputs) → storefront #/product/2 and #/category/TOBACCO
evidence:
On row 2 (White Owl cigarillos) the name and brand were cleared, price set to -5 and Save clicked.
- The browser sent PATCH /rest/v1/products?id=eq.2 {"name":"","brand":"","price":-5,"tag":null,"active":true}.
- The table showed an empty name and brand and '$-5.00'.
- After a reload, the storefront #/product/2 had an empty <h1>, the price block read '$-5.00 WHOLESALE UNIT PRICE · AW-WO', and the tab title was '· · Alabama Wholesale Inc'. The Tobacco grid card showed '$-5.00'.
- A price of 99999999 was also accepted and sent.
- The inputs have no required, min or max attributes (checkValidity() is true for all of them).
- The DB has no check constraints on products.name, brand or price (initial_schema.sql:69-78), and enforce_order_item_price would price approved buyers' lines at round(-5 × (1 − discount), 2), a negative value (launch_order_boundaries.sql:111).

Clearing the price to null is a known finding and is excluded.
fix: In src/pages/admin/AdminPage.jsx (306-309, 324), keep the price input's raw string in editing state instead of calling parseFloat on every keystroke. On Save, trim and require name and brand, and require price to be a finite number >= 0 below a sensible upper limit. Show inline errors and block the save until they are fixed, and parse the number only at save time. Back this up in the database with CHECK constraints (price >= 0, name and brand not empty) so the storefront can never show an empty title or '$-5.00'.

also_seen.location: #/admin → Products → Edit → Price
also_seen.evidence: Price onChange stores parseFloat(e.target.value) (AdminPage.jsx:309). An empty field becomes NaN, and React logged 'Warning: Received NaN for the `value` attribute' plus Chrome's 'The specified value "NaN" cannot be parsed'. Save then sent PATCH products?id=eq.1 {"price":null,…} (JSON turns NaN into null), which the NOT NULL column rejects, and the error is ignored.

title: In the Products edit row, Enter doesn't save, Escape doesn't cancel, focus drops to <body> on Edit/Save/Cancel, and opening another row silently discards edits
location: #/admin → Products → Edit / Save / Cancel in the table row
viewports: all; the product name is hidden while editing at 390x844
evidence:
At 1440:
- After clicking Edit, document.activeElement is BODY (the Edit button unmounts and focus isn't moved into 'Product name').
- Typing a name and pressing Enter: 0 PATCH, the row stays in edit mode.
- Escape: still in edit mode.
- After Save: activeElement is BODY and there is no status message.
- With row 1's name changed to 'Swisher Sweets cigarillos TEST', clicking Edit on row 3 replaced the edit state. Row 1 went back to 'Swisher Sweets cigarillos', with 0 writes and no prompt.

At 390: the 720px-wide table sits in a 356px scroller. When the Save/Cancel column is in view, the Product name input is at x = −294px, so the product being edited can be identified only by its price. At 1024 the whole row fits.
fix:
1) Render a hidden <form id={`edit-${p.id}`} onSubmit={e => { e.preventDefault(); save(...) }}> outside the table. Give each input form={`edit-${p.id}`}, and make Save type="submit" form={...}, so Enter saves.
2) Add onKeyDown on the row: Escape → cancel.
3) Use a ref to focus the name input when editing starts.
4) Keep a Map of Edit-button refs by id and, after Save or Cancel, call editBtnRefs.get(id)?.focus().
5) Add a role=status region that announces 'Saved White Owl cigarillos'.
6) Before switching editing to another row, compare with the original row; if dirty, confirm('Discard changes to <name>?').
7) At ≤600px, open the ProductEditor drawer (see the Products editor finding) instead of inline editing, or make the ID and Name columns sticky: .aw-table td:nth-child(-n+2), th:nth-child(-n+2) { position: sticky; left: 0; background: inherit }.

title: Unsaved product edits and the Products search are lost on tab switch, reload or Back with no warning, and the admin tab isn't in the URL
location: #/admin → Orders / Accounts / Products tabs; browser reload and Back
evidence:
- Searched 'Swisher', clicked Edit, changed the price to 12.34, then clicked Orders and back to Products: 0 editing rows, the admin search box reset to '', 0 dialogs, 0 writes. The edit was silently thrown away.
- A dispatched beforeunload was not prevented (defaultPrevented false), so reloading or closing also drops edits silently.
- Reloading while on Products returns to the Orders tab. The hash stays '#/admin' because the tab is plain useState('orders') (AdminPage.jsx:17), and the router maps only 'admin' (App.jsx:173, 182).

1) Route admin sections as #/admin/orders, #/admin/accounts and #/admin/products. In parseHash (App.jsx:173) return { page: 'admin', section: rest[0] || 'orders', query: ... } and have routeToHash (App.jsx:182) produce it.

4) Track a dirty flag (editing differs from the original row). When dirty, confirm before a tab switch or before starting another row's edit, and add window.addEventListener('beforeunload', e => { e.preventDefault(); e.returnValue = '' }) while dirty.

title: On phones the email and address on the Contact page render at 30px and the email breaks mid-address, dwarfing the phone number
location: #/contact → EMAIL and VISIT info cards
evidence: At 390px the computed font-size of .info-lead-small is 30px/42px instead of 17px. location: SKU text on cards, PDP ("SKU …"), cart/quote lines, Quick Reorder (#/account#quick-reorder)
evidence: 108 of 368 SKUs are exactly 17 characters and cut mid-word, e.g. AW-RAZ-VUE-FULL-K, AW-PEPCID-COMPLET, AW-CHEAP-ANTIFREE, AW-HAPPY-VALENTIN, AW-DUBAI-CHOCOLAT, AW-MELTED-MUSHROO. title: Variant labels are inconsistent: mixed flavor and size axes, abbreviations, typos, merged flavors, and non-choices
location: PDP variant chips, cart/quote line names and generated variant SKUs
evidence: Flavor and size mixed in one list with inconsistent abbreviations: #162 "Almond reg" / "Almond king size"; #171 "Cookies king" vs "Milk king size"; #166 "Cups regular" vs "White cups reg"; #169 "Red reg" / "Red king size". #62 merges two flavors into one chip, "Watermelon ice Kiwi dragon berry", so the count of 8 is wrong. Cryptic or misspelled: #62 "Omg b burst"; #63 "Sour Apple ice"; #150 "IPhone", "IPhone To type C", "Type C To Type C"; #52 "Butter flies"; #51 "Apple jack"; #183 "Winter fresh" vs #38 "Winterfresh"; #12 "Cookies cream" vs #1 "Cookies & cream"; #201 "5-flavors"; #27 "AAA4", "D2"; #331 "AAA2". Unit formats: #356 "1 gal; 2gal; 5 gal"; #107 "13gal; 23gal"; #212 "8lbs; 10lbs"; #120 "20oz"; #362 "M size; L size". Order: #314 [Big; Small; Medium; 1kg]; #125 [Big; Small; Medium]. Not real choices: #122–#124 ["Case"], #329 ["Tips"], #267 ["Mix"], #258 ["Any flavor"], #330 ["Organic"], #354 ["Small"]. Packaging colors instead of attributes: #108 Tampax Yellow/Green, #134 rubbing alcohol White/Green, #132/#133 charcoal White/Red, #324 Twangerz Yellow/Green, #28 Rhino Purple/Black/Gold. Improved since the prior audit's "almond king size" example, but still inconsistent.
fix:
Normalize every variants array in src/data/products.js.
(1) Use one axis per list: split size from flavor, e.g. Hershey's bars becomes flavors [Milk, Cookies 'n' Creme, Almond, Mr. Goodbar] plus a separate size row or product for King size, or at minimum a uniform "<Flavor> — Regular" / "<Flavor> — King size".
(2) Spell sizes "Regular" and "King size", never reg/king.
(3) Fix the spellings: iPhone (Lightning), USB-C, Lightning to USB-C, USB-C to USB-C, Butterflies, Apple Jacks, Winterfresh, Cookies & cream, 5 Flavors, AAA 4-pack, AA 4-pack, D 2-pack, AAA 2-pack, AA 2-pack, C 2-pack, 1 gal, 2 gal, 5 gal, 13 gal, 23 gal, 8 lb, 10 lb, 20 oz, 16 oz, 12 oz, 8 oz, Medium, Large.
(4) Split #62's merged chip into "Watermelon ice" and "Kiwi dragon berry", and get the real name of "Omg b burst" from the owner.
(5) Order sizes Small → Medium → Big (#125, #314).
(6) For one-item non-choices (#122–124 "Case", #329 "Tips", #267 "Mix", #258 "Any flavor", #330 "Organic", #354 "Small"), set variants: [] and flavors: 0, and move the information into sellUnit or the name.
(7) Ask the owner which real attribute the packaging colors stand for (#108, #134, #132, #133, #324, #28) and use it. Do not invent values.
Add a rule in validate() at scripts/build-seed.mjs:47 that pushes a problem for any variant label matching /^I[A-Z]|\bTo\b|\b(reg|king)$|\d(gal|lbs|oz)\b/.
Renaming a label changes its slug (lines.js:10) and the generated variant SKU (lines.js:31), so keep a map from old to new labels and check that QuickReorder still resolves past orders. Finally, run `npm run seed` and apply supabase/seed/products.sql to Supabase, because the storefront reads variants from the live products table.

title: Button system is fragmented: about 15 visual button styles with different sizes, radii, casing and hover colors
location: Header (Sign Up, Cart), product cards (Choose / QUOTE + / ADD +), carousel controls, dialogs, cart drawer, account/admin
evidence: Measured signatures include: .button (12px/700, radius 2px, 44px, bg #c84716, hover #b8390a); .aw-signup 'Sign Up ↗' (13px, radius 3px, padding 10×18, hover #a93208), a second primary button that looks similar but isn't the same component; .button.ghost (12px, radius 2px, 44px, transparent); .aw-cart-btn (13px, radius 3px); .home-carousel-controls button (12px, radius 2px, 40px, white bg); .card-add (11px, 1px tracking, radius 0, 40px); .mini-btn (10px UPPERCASE, radius 0, about 29px); .sub-pill (12px/600, radius 0); .variant-chips (12px/600, radius 2px, paper bg, no hover); .dept-jump (12px/700, radius 0); .active-filters chips (radius 999px). In one card slot the labels are 'Choose' (sentence case, App.jsx:832) and 'QUOTE +' / 'ADD +' (upper case, App.jsx:840), side by side in the same grid (home-cards-1440.png). There are four close-button variants: .dialog-close (40px, paper bg, 24px ×), .aw-menu-close (40px, white bg), .drawer-remove (40px, 22px ×) and the search close (36px, 20px ×). There are three stepper variants: card 40px/18px glyph/32px value, PDP 44px/20px/44px, drawer 40px/18px/34px. wireframes/skeleton/STYLE-GUIDE.md specifies 'mostly square; buttons use 2–3 px radius'.
fix: Make .button the single button component. Variants: `.button` (primary orange), `.button.ghost` (purple outline), `.button.on-dark` (white outline, the current age-gate/contact-strip ghost), `.button.sm` (min-height 40px, padding 0 14px, 12px) and `.button.xs` (min-height 32px, 11px). Use radius 2px everywhere and sentence case. Then: header Sign Up (App.jsx:495) → `className="button aw-desktop-only"` and delete .aw-signup; Cart → `button ghost sm`; .card-add → `button ghost sm`; carousel controls → `button ghost sm`; .mini-btn → `button xs` (primary/ghost/text). Change the card labels at App.jsx:832/840 to 'Choose variant' and 'Add to quote' / 'Add to order'. Create one `.icon-btn` (40×40, radius 50%, 1px var(--line) border, white bg, 20px icon) and use it for .dialog-close, .aw-menu-close, .drawer-remove and the search-results close. Create one `.stepper` (44px buttons on touch, 40px on desktop, 20px icons, 40px value) for card, PDP and drawer.

title: A 30px purple strip shows below the FDA warning band, and the legal row sits flush on top of the band

title: Form controls use different heights, backgrounds, borders, radii and label sizes on every form, and the file inputs are unstyled native controls
location: #/quote form, sign-in/application dialogs, #/reset-password, #/category filter search + sort, #/delivery state select, account Quick Reorder, admin table
evidence: Measured controls: .form-grid input/select are 44px, bg #f8f6f2, border #dcd5cc, radius 2px, 14px. The reset form overrides the bg to #fff. .filter-search input is 44px, #fff, border #d8d1c9, radius 0. .category-sort select is 40px, #fff, #d8d1c9, radius 0, 12px. .eligibility-form select is 44px, #fff, #dcd5cc, radius 2px. The header search is 48px, #f8f6f2, radius 3px (on mobile the border becomes #b9aed0). Quick-reorder inputs are 40px, #fff, #d8d1c9, radius 0, 13px. Admin table inputs are 34px, 12px. Labels: form-grid 11px/1.2px tracking, eligibility 10px, qr 9px/1.3px, sort 11px/1.3px muted, doc-upload 11px. The two document-upload fields in the application dialog show the browser's grey native 'Choose File' button inside the branded field (apply-form-dialog-bottom-1440.png). Native search inputs show the browser's default cancel '×'.
fix: Add shared field tokens and one control rule: `:root { --field-h: 44px; --field-bg: #fff; --field-border: #dcd5cc; --field-radius: 2px; }` and `.form-grid input, .form-grid select, .filter-search input, .category-sort select, .eligibility-form select, .qr-field input, .qr-choice select { height: var(--field-h); background: var(--field-bg); border: 1px solid var(--field-border); border-radius: var(--field-radius); font-size: var(--text-base); }` (compact 34px only inside .aw-table). Give every label the .form-grid label style (11px, 1.2px tracking, purple). Style the file button: `.doc-file::file-selector-button { margin-right: 12px; padding: 8px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--purple); background: #fff; color: var(--purple); font: 700 var(--text-sm) var(--body); border-radius: 2px; cursor: pointer; }`. Hide the native search cancel with `input[type=search]::-webkit-search-cancel-button { -webkit-appearance: none; }` and provide a styled clear button if one is needed.

title: Form inputs are 12–14px on phones, which makes iOS Safari zoom the page when a field is focused
location: #/quote (all 11 fields), sign-in/application/reset dialogs, #/category filter drawer (search 14px, sort 12px), #/delivery state select
evidence: Measured at 390px with a mobile UA: quote-business, contact, email, phone, street, city, state, zip, delivery select, date and notes are all 14px. aw-email and aw-pass in the sign-in dialog are 14px. category-search is 14px and category-sort 12px. delivery-state is 14px. Only the header search is raised to 16px (index.css:538). iOS Safari auto-zooms into any focused field under 16px, which breaks the layout mid-form on the checkout and application flows.
fix: Set font-size to at least 16px on all inputs, selects and textareas at phone widths (the quote form, auth dialogs, #/reset-password, file inputs, category filter search/sort, #/delivery select, Quick Reorder SKU/Qty), so iOS Safari doesn't zoom on focus (index.css:270, 381, 445, 538, 594, 800).

also_seen.location: Auth modal forms and #/reset-password form on phones
also_seen.evidence: Measured at 390px: computed font-size is 14px on every .form-grid input/select (#aw-su-name … #aw-su-volume, #aw-email, #aw-pass) and 12px on .doc-file. iOS Safari auto-zooms inputs under 16px on focus, which shifts the fixed dialog sideways. title: The hero carousel ignores swipes on phones
location: #/ → hero carousel stage (.home-carousel-stage)
viewports: Phones and tablets (tested 390x844 touch in Chromium and WebKit)
evidence:
Autoplay was paused (reduced motion) so that only a gesture could change the slide.
- Chromium: a real CDP touch swipe across the stage (touchStart at x=330 → touchMove ×10 → touchEnd at x=40, then the reverse) left 'Slide 1 of 4' unchanged both ways, with scrollY still 0.
- WebKit: synthetic touch-type pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup across the stage left 'Slide 1 of 4' unchanged. (WebKit on macOS rejects the Touch constructor, so real TouchEvents could not be sent.)
- src/App.jsx has no onTouch*, onPointer* or swipe handling (grep found only an onFocus on the search input). The stage is not a scroll container either: overflow-x visible, scroll-snap-type none, scrollWidth equals clientWidth (356).

On a phone the only way to change slides is the small text buttons below the image, and on WebKit those are partly covered by the photo (see the Safari carousel finding).
fix: In HeroCarousel (src/App.jsx:623-697), add swipe handling to the stage div at :661. Store the start point in a ref in onPointerDown={e => (start.current = { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY })}. In onPointerUp, compute dx and dy; if Math.abs(dx) > 40 && Math.abs(dx) > Math.abs(dy), call go(dx < 0 ? 1 : -1) and setPaused(true) so autoplay doesn't immediately move it again. Clear start.current in onPointerCancel. Add `touch-action: pan-y;` to `.home-carousel-stage` in src/index.css:178 so vertical page scrolling still works and horizontal swipes reach the handlers. Alternatively, rebuild the stage as an overflow-x: auto track with scroll-snap-type: x mandatory and sync the index from scroll position.

title: Header search isn't exposed as a combobox: arrow keys do nothing and Enter jumps to an unseen first result
location: Header search (all routes)
evidence:
The input has no role, aria-expanded, aria-controls or aria-autocomplete. After typing 'backwoods' ('3 results'), ArrowDown leaves focus in the input. Tab order is input → Search button → 'Close search results' → results, so results are reached only after two unrelated stops. Pressing Enter (submitSearch) opens the first hit's product page without saying which product that is. The

result count is mounted together with the results container, so the first count is often not announced. Results don't close on blur (see the focus-obscured finding).
fix: Implement the header search as an ARIA 1.2 combobox: role='combobox', aria-expanded, aria-controls, listbox/option roles, aria-activedescendant, and ArrowUp/Down/Home/End/Escape handling. Enter selects the highlighted option, or goes to a results page when nothing is highlighted (App.jsx:437, 459-465).

also_seen.location: Header search input and results dropdown (.aw-search-results)
also_seen.evidence: With 'geek bar' typed, ArrowDown and ArrowUp left focus in the input and highlighted nothing. Results can only be reached by pressing Tab past the Search button and the 'Close search results' button; the first result is the third Tab stop. The input has no role='combobox', aria-expanded, aria-controls, aria-autocomplete or aria-activedescendant, and the list has no listbox or option roles. The '10 results' role='status' element is created at the same moment as its text, so screen readers often don't announce the first result count.

title: Carousel autoplay pushes homepage LCP to 7–13 s because later slides paint larger
location: #/ → HeroCarousel autoplay (4.5 s interval)
viewports: all (measured 412 mobile throttled, 390 mobile and 1440 desktop unthrottled)
evidence: The production build was served with vite preview. Mobile (412x823, DPR 1.75, 4x CPU, slow-4G) LCP entries: text 2.6 s, then hero_candy at 3.4 s, then hero_vape at 7.0 s (2 runs: 6,996/6,964 ms). The last entry is the reported LCP. Unthrottled with no user input: desktop 1440 went hero_candy 100 ms, then hero_lighters at 9,068 ms; mobile 390 went hero_candy 100 ms, then hero_vape at 4,560 ms, then hero_gatorade at 13,560 ms. Cause: slides render at intrinsic size, so painted areas differ (desktop: candy 308,700px², lighters 336,700px²; mobile: candy 79,744, vape 126,736, gatorade 138,484). Each autoplay advance to a larger slide becomes a new, later LCP candidate. With prefers-reduced-motion (autoplay off) LCP stays at hero_candy, 3.5 s. The homepage is the only indexable URL, so this is the Core Web Vitals score Google records for the site.
fix: 1) Give every slide the same painted box. Apply the overflow fix (img width:100%; height:100%; object-fit:contain inside a fixed-height stage). Also re-export all four hero sources (src/assets/hero_*.jpg) to one identical canvas, e.g. 1440x900 letterboxed on white, so no later slide is larger than slide 1. 2) Don't start the 4.5 s interval (App.jsx:651-655) until the user has interacted: set a `userInteracted` flag on the first pointerdown/keydown/scroll listener and add it to the effect's condition. Alternatively, initialise `paused` to true and autoplay only after interaction. 3) Re-measure: LCP should stay on slide 1 at about 3.4 s on slow-4G mobile.

title: Fallback fonts don't match the web fonts: the font swap causes CLS 0.17 on product pages, and headings fall back to synthetic-bold Impact or a wide system sans when Barlow Condensed is blocked or loading
location: #/product/61 (and any product whose breadcrumb wraps in the fallback font); all pages when fonts swap
evidence: Production build, 412x823 mobile, 4x CPU, slow-4G: CLS on #/product/61 was 0.1704 in both runs (Core Web Vitals threshold 0.1), with a single shift at about 4.28 s. Source: .pd-grid moved from y=304.5 to y=280 and the crumb span from 270 to 235.75. With .woff2 requests blocked, CLS was 0.0000, so the font swap is the cause. The 11px/700 breadcrumb "HOME / NOVELTIES & VAPES / GEEK BAR PULSE X 25K" measures 339px in the Verdana fallback against 280px in DM Sans, so it wraps to 2 lines (60.5px) and snaps to 1 line (36px) when DM Sans arrives. The fonts are discovered late: nothing preloads them, and @font-face files are only requested after React renders. DM Sans starts at 2,468 ms and finishes at 4,196 ms; Barlow 700 finishes at 3,616 ms. The main JS finishes at 2,377 ms. Four static Barlow weights (500/600/700/800, about 14.8 KB each) are bundled.
fix: Preload the display and body woff2 files in index.html. Define metric-matched fallback @font-face rules (e.g. local('Arial Narrow') / local('Arial') with size-adjust, ascent-override and descent-override) for --display and the body font (index.css:4, 22-23; fonts.css:4-38). Remove Impact and Verdana from the font stacks.

also_seen.location: All h1/h2/h3, .pd-price b, .info-lead, age-gate h1 → var(--display) when the Barlow Condensed woff2 is blocked or still loading
also_seen.evidence:
The bundled .woff2 fonts were blocked and CDP CSS.getPlatformFontsForNode read the rendered face on each platform:
- macOS: Arial Narrow + Verdana, close to the design.
- Windows without Office (no Arial Narrow): Impact. Its only weight is regular, so h1-h3 at font-weight 700 are faux-bolded. 'Contact & visit' and the '(205) 354-4473' lead number render as a crushed, heavy poster face.
- iOS and Android (neither Arial Narrow nor Impact installed): generic sans (Helvetica/Roboto), which is much wider. The Collections H2 'Disposables, detox, kratom & more.' wraps to 3 lines at 390, and the PDP 'Sign in' price block widens from 82px to 95px (Impact) and 113px (sans).
The header survives: at 1024 and 1440 the nav row stays 55px and the masthead 106px in every scenario, and no horizontal overflow was found. Account actions widen from 272px to 295px under Verdana.
This fallback shows permanently when web fonts are blocked (corporate filters, data savers) and on every first visit during the swap window: Barlow arrived about 250ms after first render on Fast 3G. This is separate from the known CLS finding, which measured shift, not the fallback face.

title: One 638 KB main JS chunk with no code splitting; 46% unused on home, first paint 2.6 s on slow 4G
location: Production build: assets/index-*.js (loaded on every route)
evidence: `npx vite build` produces index-*.js at 637.76 kB (169.44 kB gzip), vendor (react-dom) at 140.87 kB (45.26 kB gzip) and CSS at 65.19 kB (12.68 kB gzip). Vite prints a >500 kB chunk warning. There is no React.lazy, dynamic import() or Suspense in src/. Main-chunk composition from the sourcemap (raw / gzip): all @supabase packages 206.6 KB / 53.3 KB, including realtime-js + phoenix (56 KB raw) that the app never uses; src/data/products.js 119.4 KB / 27.0 KB; inlined image data and URL imports 94.4 KB / 39.2 KB; images.js 72.1 KB / 9.8 KB; App.jsx 59.9 KB / 15.9 KB; AuthModal 15.2 KB; Admin + Account + QuickReorder + DocumentUploads + documents.js 25.3 KB / 9.5 KB; the support pages about 23 KB. Chrome coverage on #/ shows 45.5% of index.js and 63.3% of vendor.js unused. The live catalog is also fetched from Supabase on every load (368 rows), duplicating the bundled products.js.

title: Eager glob of 1,278 image URLs plus 7 base64 images adds about 166 KB (49 KB gzip) to the main bundle
location: src/lib/images.js import.meta.glob → main JS chunk
evidence: images.js:16 runs `import.meta.glob('../assets/generated/*.{webp,jpg}', { eager: true, query: '?url' })` over 1,278 generated files. The built chunk contains 2,562 '/assets/...' URL strings (119 KB of text). The glob key object in images.js is 72.1 KB raw, and the URL imports are about 64 KB. Because vite.config.js:13 sets assetsInlineLimit: 4096, seven images under 4 KB are base64-inlined into the JS (27.7 KB): p150-phone-cables 320w.webp, p151-white-v-neck 320w jpg+webp, p216-grinders 320w jpg+webp, p356-gas-cans 320w.webp and paper_bags_2 320w.webp. fix: 1) Set `assetsInlineLimit: 0` in vite.config.js:13 so no product image is inlined. 2) Replace the eager glob with deterministic URLs. Have scripts/build-images.mjs write outputs to public/img/v2/<base>--<w>x<h>.{webp,jpg} (bump the folder when VERSION changes). Also write a compact manifest, src/data/image-sizes.json, shaped like { "<base>": [[320,320],[640,640],[1024,1024]] }. Rewrite fromSet() in images.js to build `/img/v2/${base}--${w}x${h}.webp` strings from that manifest. Delete the GENERATED glob. 3) Serve /img/v2/* with a long max-age (see the caching finding).

title: Hashed build assets get no long-term cache headers on Netlify
location: netlify.toml (production deploy), /assets/*
evidence: netlify.toml has [build] and a single [[redirects]] rule, but no [[headers]]. Netlify's default for every file is `cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. So on every repeat visit the browser revalidates the content-hashed JS, CSS, fonts and the ~1,280 hashed product images: 22 requests on a home load and 20 on Tobacco, each a round trip (about 560 ms RTT on slow 4G), even though the files never change under the same name.
fix:
Append to netlify.toml:
[[headers]]
  for = "/assets/*"
  [headers.values]
    Cache-Control = "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
[[headers]]
  for = "/*.png"
  [headers.values]
    Cache-Control = "public, max-age=604800"
Keep index.html uncached (Netlify default). If images move to public/img/v2/ (see the image-URL finding), add the same immutable rule for /img/v2/*.

title: No error boundary: any render error blanks the whole site

Its fallback should show the logo, 'Something went wrong loading this page', a 'Reload' button (window.location.reload()), a 'Go to home' link (href="#/" plus a reload) and the trade-desk phone/email from COMPANY. Wrap <App/> with it in src/main.jsx. Also wrap the route switch inside <main> in App.jsx:315-341 with a second boundary using key={routeToHash(route)}, so one broken page does not remove the header and footer and navigating away resets it.

title: Malformed percent-encoding in the hash crashes the router
location: #/category/<bad>, #/product/<bad> (e.g. a truncated shared link)
evidence: parseHash calls decodeURIComponent on raw segments (App.jsx:169-170) with no try/catch. Fresh load of #/category/%E0 or #/product/%E0%A4%A gives a blank page (URIError: URI malformed; #root has 0 children). While already in the app, setting location.hash='#/category/%E0' from #/category/CANDIES throws inside the hashchange listener: the URL changes but the page and title stay on 'Candies', so URL and content disagree. A link cut off mid-escape by an SMS or email client (e.g. …/DRINKS%20%2) triggers this.
fix: Wrap decodeURIComponent in the hash router in try/catch and fall back to the not-found route on malformed percent-escapes (for example #/category/%E0%A4%A), so the app doesn't crash to a blank page (App.jsx:165-186).

also_seen.location: #/category/%E0%A4%A (any route with an invalid percent escape)
also_seen.evidence: Loading http://127.0.0.1:3000/#/category/%E0%A4%A throws 'URIError: URI malformed' 3 times. React logs 'The above error occurred in the <App> component… Consider adding an error boundary', and the page is completely white: no header, no footer, no way back. decodeURIComponent is called unguarded in parseHash, which is the useState initialiser, and there is no error boundary. Truncated links pasted from chat or email can trigger this.

title: Auth loading state is ignored: signed-in users see signed-out pages and a blank checkout form
location: #/account, #/admin, #/quote on reload or direct link while signed in

title: useAuth runs as separate copies that each fetch the profile, and the profile never refreshes
location: App, AuthModal, ApplicationDocuments (#/apply for pending accounts)
evidence: useAuth is a plain hook called in App.jsx:154, AuthModal.jsx:48 and DocumentUploads.jsx:112. Each call runs its own getSession, onAuthStateChange subscription and profiles fetch. Simulated a pending account on #/apply: 2 identical GET /rest/v1/profiles?id=eq.<uid> requests (one per instance). The profile effect depends only on session.user.id (useAuth.js:46-61), so when staff approve a pending buyer who is signed in, the site keeps showing 'Pricing after approval' until a full reload or sign-out.
fix: Move auth and profile state into one AuthProvider context with a single onAuthStateChange subscription and one profile fetch, consumed by App, AuthModal and ApplicationDocuments. Add a refreshProfile (and/or realtime subscription) so approval status updates without a reload (useAuth.js:1-61).

also_seen.location: src/lib/useAuth.js used by App, AuthModal and ApplicationDocuments
also_seen.evidence: src/lib/useAuth.js:1 says 'Single source of truth', but useAuth (useAuth.js:25) is a plain hook. Each call creates its own session/profile state, calls getSession(), subscribes with onAuthStateChange (useAuth.js:39) and runs its own profiles select (useAuth.js:46-61). It is instantiated separately in App.jsx:154, AuthModal.jsx:48 and DocumentUploads.jsx:112 (ApplicationDocuments). Measured live on #/apply signed out: supabase.auth.stateChangeEmitters.size is 2 (App plus supabase-js's internal listener) and becomes 3 when the auth modal opens, so each open adds a duplicate subscription. A signed-in pending user on #/apply also mounts ApplicationDocuments, which is another instance and another profile fetch. The profile loads only when session.user.id changes (dependency array at useAuth.js:61), so a pending user whose account staff approve stays 'pending' (no prices, 'Pending' on product pages) until a full reload.

also_seen.location: src/lib/useAuth.js used by App, AuthModal and ApplicationDocuments
also_seen.evidence: useAuth() (src/lib/useAuth.js:25) holds its own state and effects. It is called in App.jsx:154 (always mounted), AuthModal.jsx:48 (mounted only while the sign-in dialog is open, App.jsx:350-354) and DocumentUploads.jsx:112 (ApplicationDocuments, mounted on #/apply for pending accounts, ApplyPage.jsx:22). Each mounted instance opens its own onAuthStateChange subscription (useAuth.js:39) and runs its own `profiles select *` (useAuth.js:49-53). The profile effect's only dependency is session?.user?.id (useAuth.js:61), so after the trade desk approves a pending account, the open storefront keeps showing 'Pricing after approval' / 'Pricing unlocks after your account is approved' (App.jsx:827, 946, 960, 1114, 1290) until a full reload. Opening the sign-in dialog meanwhile fetches a fresh profile in AuthModal's separate instance, so the dialog and the page behind it can disagree about account status.

title: Router accepts unknown and non-canonical routes: unknown paths show the homepage, and invalid or wrong-case category/sub-line URLs show a fake page with a made-up breadcrumb and '0 of 68 items'

title: Open tabs never refresh the catalog, so a long-lived tab keeps old prices, deactivated products and renamed variants until reload
location: All catalog routes, cart drawer and #/quote in a tab left open for hours
evidence:
Script pw/gap1s-14-refresh.mjs: GET /rest/v1/products fires only at page load (2 requests, from React StrictMode). There were 0 further requests after the tab was re-focused, after visibilitychange, focus and online events, and after two route changes.

Script gap1s-08-stale.mjs: a tab opened before a variant rename still lists 'Swisher Sweets cigarillos — Diamond' in its drawer and would submit it.

Server side, enforce_order_item_price (supabase/migrations/20260925120000_launch_order_boundaries.sql) raises 'Unknown variant for …' or 'Product is not available' for such lines. That fails the whole quote, which the page shows only as the generic 'We couldn't save this quote' error.

fix:
In useCatalog:
- Move the query into a `load()` function that stores lastLoadedAt.
- Call it on mount.
- Call it on document 'visibilitychange' when visibilityState === 'visible' and Date.now() - lastLoadedAt > 5 * 60 * 1000.
- Call it on window 'online'.
- Export `refresh`.

In QuotePage.handleQuoteSubmit (App.jsx:1181), await refresh() before submitOrder, then resolve the cart again. If a line disappeared or changed, stop the submit and name the affected line: 'X is no longer available — remove it or choose another variant.'

title: Network calls have no timeout: a stalled quote submit shows 'Sending…' forever, and the form and cart stay editable meanwhile
location: #/quote → 'Submit order' / 'Submit quote request'; #/account → Order history; sign-in and reset dialogs
evidence: Same setup, with the RPC held in-browser and never forwarded. Submit button 'Sending… ↗' (disabled) at 1s and 20s. No alert. 11 form controls (10 inputs + Delivery select), the line's −/+/× buttons (3) and 'Clear all items' all stay enabled. #/account 'Loading…' never resolves while the orders GET hangs. A network error on GETs is retried 3 times by postgrest-js (1s+2s+4s backoff) before the UI resolves. None of submitOrder, the account orders query, listProfileDocuments or signIn passes an AbortSignal.
fix:
1) Do NOT add a global fetch timeout in src/lib/supabase.js. supabase-js hands that fetch to storage-js too, so it would abort slow license uploads. Use per-call signals instead:
- src/lib/orders.js:13: `supabase.rpc('submit_quote', {...}).abortSignal(AbortSignal.timeout(25000))`
- src/pages/account/AccountPage.jsx:32-36: add `.abortSignal(AbortSignal.timeout(20000))` after `.order(...)`
- src/lib/documents.js:82-85 (listProfileDocuments): add the same.
2) src/App.jsx handleQuoteSubmit catch (:1199-1202): detect the timeout with `/^(AbortError|TimeoutError)\b/.test(err?.message || '')`. PostgrestError has no AbortError name. Set `submitError` to `{ before: 'This is taking longer than expected and may not have been saved. Call', after: ` before resubmitting and quote reference ${refNum}.` }`.
3) While `sending`, wrap the form grid (:1270-1287) in `<fieldset className="checkout-fieldset" disabled={sending}>` and add `.checkout-fieldset{border:0;margin:0;padding:0;min-width:0}` to index.css. Also add `disabled={sending}` to the −/+ buttons (:1256, :1258), the remove button (:1262) and 'Clear all items' (:1266).
4) AccountPage.jsx: add `const [reloadKey, setReloadKey] = useState(0)` and include it in the effect deps (:41). On error or timeout set `error`. Replace the raw message at :114 with `Couldn’t load your orders.` plus `<button className="text-link" onClick={() => { setError(null); setOrders(null); setReloadKey(k => k + 1); }}>Try again</button>`.
5) AuthModal.handleSignin (:95-101): auth-js signInWithPassword takes no AbortSignal, so race it: `await Promise.race([signIn(signin), new Promise((_, rej) => setTimeout(() => rej(Object.assign(new Error('timeout'), { code: 'timeout' })), 20000))])`. In describeError (:21), map `err.code === 'timeout'` to 'Signing in is taking too long. Check your connection and try again, or call (205) 354-4473.'

title: When the document list fails to load, a pending applicant is told both documents are 'Not uploaded'
location: #/apply (signed-in, status pending) → 'License documents' panel (.doc-panel)
evidence:
Setup (local only): a fake pending session, with the profile_documents GET answered inside the test browser.
- Request aborted (as when offline or the server errors): after the silent 1+2+4s retries, both rows show 'Not uploaded' with data-document-status="missing". No error message and no retry control.
- Same session with a tobacco_license row returned: 'Uploaded on September 20, 2026 · license.pdf'.
So during any network blip, an applicant who has already sent documents is told they are missing. That invites duplicate uploads and 'did you get my license?' calls. Cause: DocumentUploads.jsx:128 `.catch(() => { if (!cancelled) setRecords([]); })` turns a failed load into 'no records'. The status logic at :57-60 then prints 'Not uploaded'.
fix:
In ApplicationDocuments: - Add `const [loadError, setLoadError] = useState(false)`. - In the catch at :128, call `setLoadError(true)` and leave `records` as null instead of setting []. - Pass `loadError` into DocumentFields. When it is true, set the status text to 'Couldn’t check this document right now', use data-document-status="unknown" and do not add the is-missing class. - Above the fields, render `

We couldn’t load your document status.

`. `reload` re-runs listProfileDocuments.

title: RLS policy profiles_self_update lets customers rewrite any profile column (email, license, EIN, resale certificate), which also lets a customer be promoted to admin by the owner-provisioning script
location: RLS policy profiles_self_update on public.profiles (reachable from the browser with the anon key and a customer session)
evidence: profiles_self_update only blocks changes to role, status and pricing_tier. Any signed-in customer can `update profiles set license_no=…, ein=…, resale_cert_no=…, business=…, state=…, email=…` on their own row, including after approval. The status stays 'approved', so the account keeps tier pricing under a different, unverified license. The admin view shows profiles.email as the contact address (AdminPage.jsx:197), so a customer can also change where the trade desk sends replies. The storefront has no profile-edit UI (the only `from('profiles').update` is in AdminPage.jsx:175), so customers need no UPDATE rights at all. Auth email changes (`auth.updateUser({ email })`) are also never synced to profiles.email.
fix: Restrict self-updates on public.profiles to safe contact columns, using column-level GRANT UPDATE or a BEFORE UPDATE trigger that rejects changes to email, status, role, tier, license, EIN and resale certificate after submission (rls_policies.sql:22). Change supabase/seed/provision_owner.sql to match the owner by auth.users.id / auth.users.email instead of profiles.email.

also_seen.location: supabase/seed/provision_owner.sql (the owner setup step in BACKEND.md §2 and §5), RLS policy profiles_self_update
also_seen.evidence: provision_owner.sql runs `update public.profiles set role='admin', status='approved' where email = 'REPLACE_WITH_OWNER_EMAIL'`. profiles.email is a plain case-sensitive `text unique` column. The profiles_self_update policy lets a user update their own row whenever role, status and pricing_tier stay unchanged, so email is freely writable: `supabase.from('profiles').update({ email: 'Alabamawholesaleinc@gmail.com' }).eq('id', myId)` passes RLS. The business email appears publicly with a capital A in index.html:41 and content.js:11. Supabase stores auth emails in lowercase, so the owner's real profile row holds 'alabamawholesaleinc@gmail.com'. Attack: an applicant sets their profile email to the capitalised address (or to the exact address before the owner signs up, which also makes the owner's signup fail on the unique constraint). The owner then pastes the address from the site into provision_owner.sql, and the UPDATE promotes the attacker's row to approved admin. No check against auth.users or email confirmation exists. Admins created by the old first-signup trigger are also never audited by the later migration.

title: License proof is not kept or auditable after approval: documents disappear from admin, applicants can delete them, and approvals record no who or when
location: #/admin → Accounts → Documents column; storage bucket application-documents; table profile_documents
evidence: The Documents column renders only when `p.status === 'pending'` (AdminPage.jsx:219). After Approve, or after suspension, the admin can no longer see or open the license or resale proof. RLS lets the applicant delete or replace their profile_documents rows and storage objects at any time, including after approval (application_documents.sql:51-56 and 88-93). profile_documents_self_insert also has no status check. Approving only sets status (AdminPage.jsx:250). There is no approved_by, approved_at or verification note, and no history table, so the business cannot show when, by whom, or on what evidence a tobacco buyer was approved.
fix: 1) New migration: `alter table public.profiles add column approved_at timestamptz, add column approved_by uuid references public.profiles(id), add column verification_note text;`. Add a BEFORE UPDATE trigger that sets approved_at = now() and approved_by = auth.uid() when status changes to 'approved'. Create an append-only `public.profile_status_log(profile_id, old_status, new_status, changed_by, changed_at, note)` filled by an AFTER UPDATE trigger (admin-read RLS, no update or delete policies). 2) Change profile_documents_self_insert/update/delete, application_documents_owner_update and application_documents_owner_delete so they also require `exists(select 1 from public.profiles where id = auth.uid() and status = 'pending')`, which locks proof once approved. 3) In AdminPage.jsx:219 show the documents for every status, not just pending, and show approved_at / approved_by in the row.

title: The anonymous quote RPC has no rate limit, CAPTCHA, or length/format checks, so it can be used to flood the order inbox
location: #/quote guest form; RPC public.submit_quote (granted to anon)
evidence: submit_quote is `grant execute … to anon` (launch_order_boundaries.sql:256) and runs SECURITY DEFINER. It checks only that fields are non-blank, that there are 1–200 items, and that qty is at most 100000. It sets no maximum length on business, contact, email, phone, notes or the ship_* fields, does not validate email format, ZIP or state, and accepts preferred_date values in the past. It has no per-IP, per-email or per-session throttle. The guest form (App.jsx:1268-1297) has no honeypot or CAPTCHA. A script can therefore insert unlimited 200-line quotes under any business name and email. Combined with the Admin Orders tab loading only the newest 200 orders (separate finding), 200 junk quotes push every real order out of the admin view.
fix: New migration that recreates public.submit_quote with the same signature and grants. After the existing blank checks add: (a) `if length(p_business) > 200 or length(p_contact) > 120 or length(p_email) > 254 or length(p_phone) > 40 or length(coalesce(p_notes,'')) > 2000 or length(p_ship_street) > 200 or length(p_ship_city) > 100 or length(p_ship_zip) > 10 then raise exception 'A field is too long'; end if;` (b) `if btrim(p_email) !~* '^[^@[:space:]]+@[^@[:space:]]+[.][^@[:space:]]+$' then raise exception 'Enter a valid email'; end if;` (c) `if btrim(p_ship_zip) !~ '^[0-9]{5}(-[0-9]{4})?$' then raise exception 'Enter a valid ZIP code'; end if;` (d) `if upper(btrim(p_ship_state)) !~ '^[A-Z]{2}$' then raise exception 'Use the 2-letter state code'; end if;` (e) `if p_delivery = 'delivery' and upper(btrim(p_ship_state)) not in ('AL','MS','GA') then raise exception 'Delivery routes cover AL, MS and GA — choose will-call'; end if;`. Do not restrict the state for will-call. (f) `if p_preferred_date is not null and p_preferred_date < (now() at time zone 'America/Chicago')::date then raise exception 'Choose a date from today on'; end if;`. Throttle: `create table public.quote_throttle(key text not null, created_at timestamptz not null default now()); alter table public.quote_throttle enable row level security;` (no policies). Inside submit_quote: `v_key := coalesce(auth.uid()::text, coalesce(btrim(split_part(current_setting('request.headers', true)::json->>'x-forwarded-for', ',', 1)), 'unknown') || ':' || lower(btrim(p_email)));`, then `if (select count(*) from public.quote_throttle where key = v_key and created_at > now() - interval '15 minutes') >= 5 then raise exception 'Too many quote requests — please call the trade desk'; end if; insert into public.quote_throttle(key) values (v_key);`. Client (src/App.jsx:1268-1297): add a visually hidden honeypot input (name="company_website", tabIndex={-1}, autoComplete="off", aria-hidden) and skip submission when it is filled. Add maxLength 200/120/254/40 to business/contact/email/phone, 200 to street, 100 to city, 2 plus pattern="[A-Za-z]{2}" to state, pattern="[0-9]{5}(-[0-9]{4})?" to ZIP, 2000 to notes, and min set to today's date (YYYY-MM-DD) on the date input. Optionally, for guests, add Cloudflare Turnstile verified in an Edge Function that calls submit_quote with the service role, then revoke execute on submit_quote from anon.

title: Admin Orders tab loads only the newest 200 orders and its filter counts are wrong beyond that; Accounts has no paging
location: #/admin → Orders (status pills 'new (n)', 'all (n)'); #/admin → Accounts
evidence: OrdersTab queries `.order('created_at', { ascending: false }).limit(200)` (AdminPage.jsx:69-74) and computes pill counts from that array (AdminPage.jsx:97). With more than 200 orders, older 'new' orders vanish silently and counts under-report. The UI says nothing about truncation. AccountsTab selects every profile with no limit, status filter or paging (AdminPage.jsx:141), so above PostgREST's default max-rows (1000) accounts are cut off silently. Pending applications are also mixed in with everyone else.
fix: Add server-side pagination (range + count: 'exact') to the #/admin Orders, Accounts and Products tables. Compute the status pill counts with separate count queries, not from the loaded 200 rows. Stop claiming the list shows 'all' (AdminPage.jsx:69-141, 281-303).

also_seen.location: #/admin → Orders → status pills
also_seen.evidence: OrdersTab fetches .limit(200) (AdminPage.jsx:73) and computes 'new (n) / contacted (n) / … / all (n)' from those 200 rows (line 97). Once there are more than 200 orders, older 'new' orders disappear from the admin view and the counts are wrong, with no pagination or notice.

also_seen.location: #/admin → Products tab
also_seen.evidence: src/pages/admin/AdminPage.jsx:303 renders `filtered.slice(0, 200)`. The note at :292 says '{filtered.length} of {rows.length} products' ('368 of 368 products'), which implies everything is listed. The only disclosure, 'Showing first 200 — narrow the search to see others.', is at :346, below all 200 rows. Search (:281–285) matches only name, brand and SKU, not id or category, so an admin cannot jump to e.g. id 250 by number. Found by source review; the admin UI requires sign-in.

title: Every quote-save failure shows one generic message and cites a reference that was never saved
location: #/quote → submit error box
evidence: handleQuoteSubmit (App.jsx:1199-1202) replaces every error except code 'unavailable' with 'We couldn't save this quote. Please call … and reference ALW-Q-xxxxx.' submit_quote raises specific, customer-actionable messages that are thrown away: 'Choose a variant for <product>', 'Product is not available' (item deactivated by admin or stale static catalog), 'Invalid quantity' (qty over 100000 from a hand-edited cart), 'A ship-to address is required', 'This quote was already submitted' (double click or retry after a lost response), 'Too many items'. The cited reference does not exist in the database, so staff cannot find it.
fix: Surface the submit_quote validation messages to the user, mapped to friendly text, instead of one generic error. Don't show a reference number unless the save succeeded (App.jsx:1199-1202; orders.js:32).

also_seen.location: #/quote → submit error message
also_seen.evidence: submit_quote raises specific, user-fixable errors: 'Invalid quantity' (qty > 100000), 'Choose a variant for %', 'Unknown variant for %', 'Product is not available' (deactivated since it was carted), 'A ship-to address is required', 'Too many items' (>200 lines), 'This quote was already submitted'. The catch block (App.jsx:1199-1203) ignores err.message and always shows 'We couldn’t save this quote. Please call … and reference ALW-Q-…', so a buyer with one discontinued item cannot tell which line to remove.

title: Suspended accounts can still submit quotes, although the site tells them ordering is paused
location: #/quote and cart drawer for a profile with status 'suspended'
evidence: AuthModal.jsx:179 and ApplyPage.jsx:81 say 'Ordering is paused on this account'. isApprovedBuyer is false for suspended profiles, so the cart shows 'Request quote' (App.jsx:1432) with the wrong note 'Pricing unlocks when your account is approved' (App.jsx:1386/1426), and QuotePage enables 'Submit quote request' (App.jsx:1296). submit_quote never reads the caller's profile status, so the quote is saved under the suspended user_id. Only pricing is withheld (enforce_order_item_price, launch_order_boundaries.sql:106-113).
fix: At the top of submit_quote add: `if auth.uid() is not null and exists (select 1 from public.profiles where id = auth.uid() and status = 'suspended') then raise exception using message = 'This account is on hold', hint = 'account_suspended'; end if;`. In App.jsx derive `const isSuspended = profile?.status === 'suspended'` and pass it to CartDrawer and QuotePage. Replace the Request quote/Submit buttons with the 'Ordering is paused — call the trade desk' message and a tel: link, and change the drawer note for suspended accounts.

title: Admin saves and loads ignore Supabase errors, so failed approvals or price edits look like they worked
location: #/admin → Orders status select, Accounts status/tier/role selects and Approve, Products Edit → Save
evidence: updateStatus (AdminPage.jsx:78-81), updateProfile (174-177) and save (273-277) call `await supabase.from(...).update(...)`, never read `{ error }`, and then reload. When RLS rejects the write (session expired, admin demoted, admin's is_admin false) or a constraint fails, the select snaps back with no message. Clearing the Price input makes `parseFloat('')` NaN (AdminPage.jsx:309), which serialises to null and violates `price not null`, and this fails silently. Loads also drop errors: OrdersTab and AccountsTab do `.then(({ data }) => set(data || []))` (74, 141, 269), so a failed load shows 'No orders in this state.' instead of an error.
fix: Check { error } on every admin Supabase call (orders status, accounts status/tier/role/Approve, product Save, and loads). Show an error toast and keep the attempted value, or roll back visibly, instead of silently snapping back (AdminPage.jsx:68-78, 140-141).

also_seen.location: #/admin → Orders status select, Accounts selects / Approve, Products Save
also_seen.evidence: updateStatus (AdminPage.jsx:78-81), updateProfile (:174-177) and save (:273-277) await supabase …update() without reading { error }, then reload. The reload queries (:68-75, :141, :269) also ignore errors. When RLS rejects a write or the network fails, the select snaps back with no message, and 'Approve' appears to do nothing.

also_seen.location: #/admin → Orders status select, Accounts status/tier/role selects and Approve, Products Save
also_seen.evidence: updateStatus, updateProfile and save (AdminPage.jsx:78-81, :174-177, :273-277) await supabase.update() and ignore { error }. All three reload functions do .then(({ data }) => set(data || [])) and swallow load errors too, so a failed load looks like 'No orders in this state' or '0 of 0 products'. Simulated an admin locally with all writes aborted: changing ALW-Q-48213 to 'fulfilled' snapped the select back to 'new' with no alert, and Save on a product closed the edit row showing the old value with no message.

title: Admin role can be granted or removed, including on yourself, with one dropdown change and no confirmation
location: #/admin → Accounts → Role select
evidence: The Role `<select>` calls `updateProfile(p.id, { role: e.target.value })` on change (AdminPage.jsx:212-217). A mis-click or keyboard arrow on a customer row grants full admin, which exposes every order, EIN and license document to that customer. The same control on the admin's own row demotes them immediately and locks them out. Status 'suspended' is also one click away. No confirmation dialog, undo or audit record exists.
fix: Add a confirmation step for role/status changes in the #/admin Accounts table (especially granting or removing admin), and block admins from demoting or suspending themselves (AdminPage.jsx:199-213).

also_seen.location: #/admin → Accounts → Role select
also_seen.evidence: The Role <select> calls updateProfile(p.id, { role: e.target.value }) immediately on change (AdminPage.jsx:213-216). There is no confirmation or guard against the signed-in admin removing their own admin role, which would lock them out of #/admin.

also_seen.location: #/admin → Accounts table → Role / Status selects
also_seen.evidence: The Role select (AdminPage.jsx:213-216) calls updateProfile(p.id, { role }) on change. One mis-click or a keyboard arrow on a focused select promotes a customer to admin, or demotes the signed-in owner (including their own row) and immediately locks them out of #/admin. Status changes to 'suspended' are also instant (line 199).

title: Live catalog loading has no loading or error state and silently falls back to the bundled static catalog; there is no row cap handling
location: All catalog routes (#/, #/catalog, #/category/*, #/product/*), cart and #/quote
evidence: useCatalog now loads the live products table (the prior audit's 'storefront ignores admin catalog' is partly fixed). If that request errors, returns 0 rows or is slow, it keeps STATIC_PRODUCTS without notice (useCatalog.js:22). The static list still contains items an admin deactivated and the original names and prices. Buyers can add them, and submit_quote then rejects the whole quote with 'Product is not available', which reaches them as the generic error (see the separate finding). The first paint always uses static data, so admin price or name edits flash old values first. The comment at useCatalog.js:24-25 says 'The products table has no description or sell-unit columns yet', but the live response already includes description and sell_unit.
fix: Make useCatalog return {products, status, error} (useCatalog.js:13-24). Show a loading state, and a visible error with a retry option, instead of silently switching to the static catalog. If stale data is kept, label it and block quote submission against stale prices. Page through Supabase results or set an explicit range so the catalog isn't truncated at the default row limit.

also_seen.location: src/lib/useCatalog.js (all catalog pages)
also_seen.evidence: useCatalog swallows errors and empty results silently (useCatalog.js:22) and exposes no loading/ready flag. A product that exists only in the DB, e.g. #/product/369 in the mocked test, first renders 'Product not found' with that title until the fetch returns. select('*') is unpaginated, so PostgREST's default max-rows (1000) will silently truncate the catalog once it grows. It also pulls every column, including updated_at and price, for anonymous visitors.

title: No security headers are configured for the Netlify deploy (CSP, clickjacking protection, nosniff, HSTS, Referrer-Policy)
location: netlify.toml (production responses for every route, including #/admin)
evidence: netlify.toml holds only [build], [build.environment] and the SPA redirect. It has no [[headers]] block, and public/ has no _headers file. Production pages will therefore go out without Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or Strict-Transport-Security. The admin dashboard (approve accounts, grant admin via one select change) can be framed by another site for clickjacking. Supabase session tokens live in localStorage ('aw-auth'), so any future XSS would have no CSP backstop. The app loads no third-party scripts, iframes or fonts (fonts are bundled), so a strict 'self' policy is feasible. Hashed /assets/* files also get no long-lived Cache-Control.
fix:
Append to netlify.toml: `[[headers]]
  for = "/*"
  [headers.values]
    Content-Security-Policy = "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob: https://<project-ref>.supabase.co; font-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://<project-ref>.supabase.co wss://<project-ref>.supabase.co; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'"
    X-Frame-Options = "DENY"
    X-Content-Type-Options = "nosniff"
    Referrer-Policy = "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
    Permissions-Policy = "camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=()"
    Strict-Transport-Security = "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
[[headers]]
  for = "/assets/*"
  [headers.values]
    Cache-Control = "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"`. Replace <project-ref> with the real Supabase host. Test a deploy preview for CSP console errors before promoting it.

owner_question: Create a Cloudflare Turnstile site, enable CAPTCHA in Supabase Authentication > Attack Protection with its secret key, and give Cursor the public site key.
title: Trade signup has no bot protection (no CAPTCHA or honeypot), and password strength is enforced only in the browser
location: Apply for a trade account dialog (AuthModal signup form); Supabase Auth settings
evidence: Live DOM of the Apply dialog (#/apply → Start application): inputs name, organization, email, tel, new-password, business_type, ein, state, license_no, resale_cert_no, tobacco_license (file), resale_certificate (file) and expected_volume. There are 0 iframes, no captcha/turnstile/hcaptcha/recaptcha markup outside the dead Netlify forms, and no hidden or honeypot input. supabase.auth.signUp is called without options.captchaToken (useAuth.js:67-73). The public /auth/v1/settings shows disable_signup:false, so self-signup is open. Supabase's default per-IP rate limits slow a single-IP flood, but a distributed bot can still create many pending profiles. Each profile lands in the unfiltered Accounts tab (AdminPage.jsx:141, 193) and, once confirmed, can upload files. The password minimum of 8 exists only in the browser: minLength at AuthModal.jsx:246 and the JS check at ResetPasswordPage.jsx:23. The server minimum could not be read from public settings, and Supabase defaults to 6. BACKEND.md does not mention CAPTCHA, password policy, rate-limit or custom-SMTP settings.
fix: 1) In Supabase → Authentication → Attack Protection, enable CAPTCHA with Cloudflare Turnstile. 2) Add a small <Turnstile> wrapper component that loads https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js and returns a token via callback. Render it in all three AuthModal forms: sign-in (AuthModal.jsx:190-205), signup (:231-279) and reset (:323-334). Keep each submit button disabled until a token exists, and reset the widget after every attempt. 3) In src/lib/useAuth.js pass `options: { captchaToken }` to signInWithPassword (line 80), signUp (line 67, merged with the existing options.data) and resetPasswordForEmail (line 95, alongside redirectTo). 4) If you adopt the CSP from AW-205, add https://challenges.cloudflare.com to script-src and frame-src. 5) Under Authentication → Providers → Email, set the minimum password length to 8 (matching the UI) and enable leaked-password protection if the plan allows it. Configure custom SMTP so confirmation emails are not throttled by the built-in sender. 6) Add a 'Security settings' checklist to BACKEND.md §5 (around line 78) covering CAPTCHA, password length, rate limits and SMTP.

title: Document storage layout is not enforced on the server: storage_path is client-chosen, and users can upload unlimited files
location: Storage bucket application-documents policies; table profile_documents
evidence: The storage insert/update policies check only that the first folder equals auth.uid() (application_documents.sql:60-76). Any confirmed signup can PUT any number of 10 MB objects under `{uid}/anything/…`, so storage cost is unbounded, and the document_type subfolder is not enforced. profile_documents.storage_path is written by the client (documents.js:126-135) with no check tying it to `{profile_id}/{document_type}/` (application_documents.sql:22-30). A user can point their row at an arbitrary path, which the admin then signs and opens, or reserve a path through the UNIQUE constraint. uploadProfileDocument uploads before writing the row and ignores errors from removing the old file (documents.js:120-140), which leaves orphaned objects.
fix: Tighten the application-documents storage and profile_documents policies: require storage_path to start with auth.uid()/, cap files per user, and block insert/update/delete by the applicant after approval (application_documents.sql:22-67).

also_seen.location: supabase/migrations/20260927180000_application_documents.sql policies
also_seen.evidence: 20260927180000_application_documents.sql:48-53: `profile_documents_self_insert … with check (auth.uid() = profile_id)` and `profile_documents_self_update … with check (auth.uid() = profile_id)`. Nothing checks that storage_path starts with `${auth.uid()}/${document_type}/`. With the unique storage_path constraint (line 25), any authenticated user can insert a row claiming the path `<otherUserId>/tobacco_license/<name>` before that user uploads, and the victim's later upsert (documents.js:133-136) then fails with a unique violation. That requires the victim's UUID and filename, so real-world risk is low. Owners can also insert or replace documents via the API after approval, and the admin Accounts tab only renders documents for status 'pending'.

title: Admin 'View' links are signed for every document on load and expire after 10 minutes, leaving dead links on screen
location: #/admin → Accounts → Documents → View
evidence: On load, AccountsTab mints a signed URL for every profile_documents row, one request at a time, including rows for approved accounts whose documents are never shown (AdminPage.jsx:146-160). Each URL is valid for 600 seconds (documents.js:159). After 10 minutes the rendered `<a href>` links (AdminPage.jsx:229-233) still point at expired URLs, and clicking one opens a Supabase error page. The fallback button path that re-signs on click (viewDocument) is only used when no pre-signed URL exists.
fix: Don't pre-sign document URLs on load. Generate the signed URL on click of 'View' (short expiry), then open it (AdminPage.jsx:146, 229; documents.js:157-159).

also_seen.location: #/admin → Accounts → Documents → View
also_seen.evidence: AccountsTab creates a signed URL for every document at load (AdminPage.jsx:146-160), one request after another, with a 600 s TTL (documents.js:159). Once a URL exists, it renders a plain <a href={signedUrl}> (AdminPage.jsx:229-233) instead of the button that mints a fresh URL. A rep who opens the tab and clicks View 10+ minutes later gets Supabase's expired-token JSON error.

also_seen.location: #/admin → Accounts → Documents → View
also_seen.evidence: AccountsTab signs a URL for every document on load, one at a time (AdminPage.jsx:146-160), with a 600-second lifetime (documents.js:159), and renders them as plain <a href> links (AdminPage.jsx:229-233). After the tab has been open for 10 minutes, 'View' opens Supabase's expired-token error. Every approve or tier change calls reload(), which re-signs every document again (N sequential storage requests).

title: No test, lint or CI safety net on any branch, while many unreviewed commits and Cursor merges sit ahead of main
location: Repository root: package.json scripts, no eslint/vitest/playwright config, no .github/workflows
evidence: package.json:7–15 defines only images, seed, predev, dev, prebuild, build and preview; there is no lint, test or typecheck script. None of these exist on HEAD or on any of the 7 branches (main, redesign/2a-editorial and four remote cursor/* branches): eslint or prettier config, vitest/jest/playwright config, *.test.* or *.spec.* files, a .github/ folder, PropTypes, or TypeScript. HEAD d19d7dc is 46 commits ahead of origin/main and 0 behind. Four Cursor branches were merged within 53 seconds on 2026-09-27 04:26:35–04:27:28 UTC (ea4feb0, 44868f3, 376c8a8, 23b062b) with no automated check. I ran ESLint 9 with eslint-plugin-react-hooks on a scratchpad copy of src/.
